headnotes.la: …t, ut physici ferunt, si semel conjugem casu perdiderit, alium non requirere, sed castimoniam servans vidua quodammodo permanere, solitarius ingemiscens, atque poenitens: de quo in eodem libro legitur
headnotes.en: …eport, that if once she has by mischance lost her mate, she does not seek another, but keeping chastity remains in a manner a widow, groaning alone and doing penance: of which we read in the same book

headnotes.la: id est Christi dicentis
headnotes.en: that is, of Christ saying

headnotes.la: …t, cum plures haberet in monarchia doctores qui honeste et catholice tractare potuissent. Sed censuram imperii vestri considerans, tacitoque pertractans illud apostolicum quo dicitur [n: (I Petr. II)]
headnotes.en: … monarchy many doctors who could have handled it honorably and catholicly. But considering the censure of your rule, and silently turning over that apostolic word by which it is said [n: (I Petr. II)]

headnotes.la: , sed et potius illud Dominicum, ubi pollicetur
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *propter Deum*, "for God's sake"] , but rather that word of the Lord's, where he promises

headnotes.la: …locis ob tuam consolationem subnectere decrevimus, ne solummodo allegoriarum allusionibus pressus, violenter vestra celsitudo theorica legendo fastidiat. Audiat etiam quod per eumdem Salomonem dicitur
headnotes.en: …olation, lest, pressed down by the allusions of the allegories alone, your highness should violently grow weary in reading contemplative things. Let him also hear what is said through the same Solomon

headnotes.la: …e sequitur: et gloria regum investigare sermonem. Qui enim non solummodo regnat terrarum, sed corpora sua, vel motus carnis regere et investigare noverunt, reges sunt. Quibus et per Psalmistam dicitur
headnotes.en: …t a speech." For they who not only reign over lands, but have known how to rule and to search out their own bodies, or the motions of the flesh, are kings. To whom it is also said through the Psalmist

headnotes.la: …alomonem Scripturae manifestissime docent. *Salomonem,* id est *pacificum,* eo quod in pace regnum obtinuerit, et per parabolas populum erudierit, in significationem Salvatoris qui discipulis suis ait
headnotes.en: … was called by three names. *Solomon,* that is, *peaceable,* because he obtained the kingdom in peace and instructed the people by parables, as a signification of the Savior, who says to his disciples

headnotes.la: Et ipse per parabolas turbas docuit, de quo etiam scriptum est
headnotes.en: And he himself taught the crowds by parables, of whom also it is written

headnotes.la: et reliqua. Et *Idida,* id est *dilectus Domini,* videlicet quia prius a Domino dilectus fuerit, similiter in typum Domini qui a Patre dilectus est, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: and the rest. And *Idida,* that is, *beloved of the Lord,* namely because he was first beloved by the Lord, likewise as a type of the Lord who is beloved by the Father, as he himself says

headnotes.la: …num, sed ad universos generaliter dirigatur, qui velut extensa manu omnium tumultus sedat, eosque ad unam sententiam revocat. Sic idem Salomon in hoc libro fecisse ostenditur, cum in libri termino ait
headnotes.en: …nerally to all; who as with hand outstretched quiets the tumults of all and calls them back to one judgment. So the same Solomon is shown to have done in this book, when at the end of the book he says

headnotes.la: illum praefigurans qui non solum pacem intulit, et dilectus Deo Patri exstitit, sed qui omnibus ait
headnotes.en: prefiguring him who not only brought in peace and stood forth beloved of God the Father, but who says to all

headnotes.la: qui
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *appropinquavit*, "hath drawn near"] — who,

headnotes.la: …tico canticorum amplexibus jungit. Nisi enim prius reliquimus vitia, et pompis saeculi renuntiantes, expeditos nos ad adventum Christi paraverimus, non poterimus cantare Canticum canticorum, et dicere
headnotes.en: …. For unless we have first left our vices, and, renouncing the pomps of the world, have made ourselves unencumbered for the coming of Christ, we shall not be able to sing the Song of Songs, and to say

headnotes.la: …ita ethnicam, physicam, et theoriam nominaverunt. Unde non abhorret ab intellectu, quia liber iste in opusculis Salomonis tertio loco ponitur. In proverbiis itaque moralis vita exprimitur, ubi dicitur
headnotes.en: …oriam.* Whence it is not repugnant to the understanding that this book is placed in the third place among the little works of Solomon. So then in Proverbs the moral life is expressed, where it is said

headnotes.la: In Ecclesiaste vero naturalis. Ibi quippe quod omnia ad fidem tendant, considerantur, dum dicitur
headnotes.en: …: Vulg. Prov. V, 1 *Fili mi, attende ad sapientiam meam*, "My son, attend to my wisdom"] But in Ecclesiastes, the natural. For there it is considered that all things tend toward faith, when it is said

headnotes.la: In Canticis autem canticorum contemplativa vita exprimitur, dum in eis ipsius Domini adventus et aspectus desideratur, cum sponsae voce dicitur
headnotes.en: But in the Song of Songs the contemplative life is expressed, while in it the coming and the sight of the Lord himself is desired, when it is said with the voice of the bride

headnotes.la: …ia cantica exhortationis et contestationis, alia cantica exsultationis, alia cantica adjutorii, alia cantica conjunctionis cum Deo. Canticum victoriae est quod Maria transito mari Rubro cecinit dicens
headnotes.en: …rtation and attestation, others songs of exultation, others songs of help, others songs of conjunction with God. The song of victory is that which Miriam sang when the Red Sea had been crossed, saying

headnotes.la: Canticum exhortationis et contestationis est quod Moyses Israelitis ad terram repromissionis propinquantibus dixit
headnotes.en: …im magnificatus est … deiecit in mare*, "gloriously magnified … cast down"] The song of exhortation and attestation is that which Moses spoke to the Israelites as they drew near to the land of promise

headnotes.la: Canticum exsultationis est quod Anna non solum pro Samuele, sed prospecta fecunditate Ecclesiae in semetipsa cecinit dicens
headnotes.en: … 1 *Audite, caeli, quae loquor; audiat terra verba oris mei*] The song of exultation is that which Anna sang, not only for Samuel, but having foreseen in herself the fruitfulness of the Church, saying

headnotes.la: Ubi per semetipsam veritas fecunditatem prolis ecclesiasticae expressit, cum dicit
headnotes.en: Where through her own self the truth expressed the fruitfulness of the ecclesiastical offspring, when she says

headnotes.la: Canticum adjutorii David post praelium cecinit dicens
headnotes.en: The song of help David sang after the battle, saying

headnotes.la: …em siquidem dicitur, quia post iracundiam omnipotentis Dei pacem de coelo missam a patre suscepit, eo quod aliquam signatur habere pacem. Quam pacem et conjunctionem exorare dicitur cum eum deprecatur
headnotes.en: … the wrath of Almighty God she received the peace sent from heaven by the Father, in that she is signified to have some peace. Which peace and conjunction she is said to entreat when she beseeches him

headnotes.la: …d annos pubertatis provecta, et ejus doctrina quasi monilibus exornata, sed ejus conjunctione usque ad regnum coelorum sublimata. Sed quomodo ignominiose et conculcata jacebat per Prophetam increpatur
headnotes.en: …of puberty, and adorned with his doctrine as with necklaces, but by his conjunction exalted even to the kingdom of heaven. But how ignominiously and trodden down she lay is rebuked through the Prophet

headnotes.la: Et qualiter per adventum suae conjunctionis facere voluit unum ex his misertus sui subjunxit
headnotes.en: …lowing, *sed proiecta es super faciem terrae in abiectione animae tuae*] And in what manner, having pity on her, he willed through the coming of his conjunction to do one of these things, he subjoined

headnotes.la: …cclesia, sed quia ornari non poterat nisi per ejus apparitionem, idcirco illius visitationem desiderabat. Audierat enim tanquam sponsa per prophetam in persona sponsi, id est Verbi Dei Patris dicentis
headnotes.en: …ed save through his appearing, therefore she desired his visitation. For she had heard, as a bride, through the prophet, in the person of the Bridegroom, that is, of the Word of God the Father, saying

headnotes.la: Et per Isaiam similiter vox ipsius Ecclesiae ait
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Ose. II, 19–20 *sponsabo* three times, and includes *et in miserationibus*] And through Isaiah likewise the voice of the Church herself says

headnotes.la: Et Zacharias hujuscemodi gloriam trepidanti Ecclesiae nuntiatam dicendo ait
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Isa. LXI, 10 lacks *Posuit mihi mitram sicut sponsae* and reads *et indumento iustitiae circumdedit me*] And Zacharias, in announcing glory of this kind to the trembling Church, says

headnotes.la: Hi ergo omnes patriarchae et prophetae, futuram, ineffabilem Christi et Ecclesiae copulam cecinere. Apostolus autem jam celebratam exposuit dicens
headnotes.en: …t super pullum filium asinae*] All these patriarchs and prophets, therefore, sang of the future, ineffable coupling of Christ and the Church. But the Apostle set it forth as already celebrated, saying

headnotes.la: Et iterum ad Corinthios
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Ephes. V, 27 *gloriosam Ecclesiam*, "a glorious Church"] And again to the Corinthians

headnotes.la: Et alio loco ita exhortatur fideles
headnotes.en: And in another place he thus exhorts the faithful

headnotes.la: …o Scriptura sacra Dominum vocat, aliquando patrem, aliquando sponsum. Quando enim vult se timeri, Dominum se nominat; quando vult honorari, patrem; quando vult amari, sponsum. Ipse per prophetam dicit
headnotes.en: …mes father, sometimes bridegroom. For when he wills to be feared, he names himself Lord; when he wills to be honored, father; when he wills to be loved, bridegroom. He himself says through the prophet

headnotes.la: Et rursum dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Mal. I, 6 *Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? et si Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus?* — the two clauses in the reverse order] And again he says

headnotes.la: …sit ejus suscipere oscula, et una cum eo effecta spiritum in coelestibus sublimata regnare. Quae sublimitas humiliatione Filii Dei celebrata cognoscitur sicut magister gentium docet de Christo dicendo
headnotes.en: …together with him, to reign exalted in the heavenly places. Which sublimity is known to have been celebrated by the humbling of the Son of God, as the teacher of the Gentiles teaches, saying of Christ

headnotes.la: …s omne genus humanum ab exordio mundi usque ad finem mundi, totam videlicet Ecclesiam unam esse personam: quae arrhas spirituali dono perceperat, sed tamen sponsi sui praesentiam quaerebat, quae dicit
headnotes.en: …ng of the world unto the end of the world — namely, that the whole Church is one person: who had received earnests by a spiritual gift, but nevertheless sought the presence of her bridegroom, who says

headnotes.la: … dulcedine praesentiae suae, quam saepius a prophetis promissam audivi. Unde et de eodem sponso in Evangelio scriptum est [n: (Matth. V)], cum sederet in monte, et sublimium praeceptorum verba faceret
headnotes.en: …promised by the prophets. Whence also concerning the same bridegroom it is written in the Gospel [n: (Matth. V)], when he was sitting on the mountain and was speaking the words of the sublime precepts

headnotes.la: … per omnes patriarchas et prophetas ad Patrem omnipotentem lacrymabili voce clamavit, ejus sibi oscula propinari, quem et in Jordanis baptismo vox Patris de nube, et Joannes digito monstravit, dicendo
headnotes.en: …h tearful voice to the Almighty Father that his kisses be brought near to her; whom, both in the baptism of Jordan the voice of the Father from the cloud, and John with his finger, pointed out, saying

headnotes.la: Et Pater ipse de nube
headnotes.en: And the Father himself from the cloud

headnotes.la: Unum autem de multis amicis sponsi praeparantem sponsam Joannem intellige, cujus praesentia Ecclesia Christi oscula sancta suscepit, ipso testante de Christo
headnotes.en: But understand John to be one of the many friends of the bridegroom preparing the bride, by whose presence the Church received the holy kisses of Christ, he himself testifying concerning Christ

headnotes.la: Miratur videlicet Joannes, cum vidit eum propter aquarum sanctificationem ad baptismum venientem, qui ait
headnotes.en: …an. III, 29 *amicus autem sponsi, qui stat et audit eum, gaudio gaudet propter vocem sponsi*] John marvels, namely, when he saw him coming to the baptism for the sanctification of the waters, who says

headnotes.la: [n: (Matth. III.)] Gaudio vero gaudet, audiens vocem ejus dicentis
headnotes.en: [n: (Matth. III.)] But he rejoices with joy, hearing the voice of him saying

headnotes.la: Ubi completae sunt preces Ecclesiae jam olim promissae ad Deum Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi dicentis
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Matth. III, 15 *sic enim decet nos*, "for so it becometh us"] Wherein were fulfilled the prayers of the Church, promised long since, to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, saying

headnotes.la: …aesentem. Habet enim gratia Redemptoris nostri, ut cum de illo quaerentes loquimur, ejus praesentia perfruamur, sic de duobus Cleopha videlicet et alio, sicut in Evangelio scriptum est. Unde subjungit
headnotes.en: …eemer has this: that when we speak of him as those who seek him, we enjoy his presence — thus it was concerning the two, namely Cleophas and the other, as is written in the Gospel. Whence she subjoins

headnotes.la: …ejus ubera laudantur, quia praedicationis ejus condescensio hoc egit in cordibus nostris, quod doctrina legis agere minime valuit. Plus enim nos nutrivit incarnationis praedicatio, quam legis doctrina
headnotes.en: …ondescension of his preaching wrought that in our hearts which the doctrine of the law was by no means able to work. For the preaching of the incarnation nourished us more than the doctrine of the law

headnotes.la: Unguenta Domini virtutes sunt. Unguentum Domini, Spiritus sanctus fuit, de quo ei per Prophetam dicitur
headnotes.en: The ointments of the Lord are the virtues. The ointment of the Lord was the Holy Spirit, concerning whom it is said to him through the Prophet

headnotes.la: … praedicatione percipientem, quae per divinam gratiam etiam ipsa illustrari desiderat, ut aliquando etiam per se intelligat, quae nihil se intelligere nisi per verba praedicatorum considerat, et dicat
headnotes.en: …res that she too be enlightened by divine grace, so that at some time she may understand even of herself; who considers that she understands nothing except through the words of preachers, and who says

headnotes.la: …non jam praedicatorum vocibus, sed internae ejus gratiae tactu perfruar. Quasi osculo oris sui osculabatur Moysen Dominus, cum per fiduciam familiaris gratiae intellectum porrigeret. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: … preachers, but the touch of his inward grace. The Lord kissed Moses as with the kiss of his mouth, when through the confidence of familiar grace he extended understanding to him. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: Os quippe ad os loqui, quasi osculari est, et interna intelligentia mente tangere. Sequitur
headnotes.en: …ione apparebo ei, vel per somnium loquar ad illum. At non talis servus meus Moyses*] For to speak mouth to mouth is, as it were, to kiss, and to touch the mind with inward understanding. There follows

headnotes.la: …spiciat, humillimam praedicationis Dominicae incarnationem appetat. Plus ei sapiat quod per infirmitatem carnis ejus nutritur, quam quod mundus hic per elationem falsae prudentiae extollitur, et dicat
headnotes.en: …Lord's preaching. Let that savor more to her whereby she is nourished through the infirmity of his flesh, than that whereby this world is exalted through the elation of false prudence; and let her say

headnotes.la: id est humillima incarnationis tuae praedicatio elatam mundi sapientiam superat. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: that is, the most humble preaching of thy incarnation surpasses the puffed-up wisdom of the world. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: …t, quia Deo placere non appetunt. Olent tamen in humanis naribus dum humano judicio bonam opinionem reddunt. Sed comparentur haec vero odori Redemptoris nostri, comparentur veris virtutibus et dicatur
headnotes.en: …ell sweet in human nostrils, while by human judgment they render a good repute. But let these be compared with the true odor of our Redeemer, let them be compared with true virtues, and let it be said

headnotes.la: …ed necdum osculantur, quia amore ejus minime compunguntur. Quod bene in convivio Pharisaei signatum est. Qui cum Dominum recepisset, cumque osculanti mulieri pedes ejus in corde suo derogaret, audivit
headnotes.en: …pricked with compunction by his love. Which was well signified in the banquet of the Pharisee. Who, when he had received the Lord, and when in his heart he disparaged the woman kissing his feet, heard

headnotes.la: …, quasi Christum in convivium recipit, Christum pascit, quia eum in membris suis sustentare non desinit. Sed si nondum per amorem compungitur, adhuc ejus vestigia non osculatur. Bene autem dictum est,
headnotes.en: …o a banquet, feeds Christ, because he does not cease to sustain him in his members. But if he is not yet pricked with compunction through love, he does not yet kiss his footsteps. But it is well said,

headnotes.la: …in amore Dei semel compungi et quiescere, sed et compunctio debet esse et crebrescere. Unde mulier in eo laudatur, quia osculari non destitit id compungi minime cessavit. Unde et per Prophetam dicitur
headnotes.en: …be and to grow frequent. Whence the woman is praised in this, that she did not cease to kiss, that is, she by no means ceased to be pricked with compunction. Whence also it is said through the Prophet

headnotes.la: …nstituitur, cum ad lacrymas prae amore Domini assidue movetur. Cur vel si diceremus quandiu ista acturi sumus, quandiu tribulationibus afficimur? illico terminum quousque fieri debeat subjunxit dicens
headnotes.en: …ove of the Lord. Wherefore, or if we should say, how long are we to do these things, how long are we afflicted with tribulations? at once he subjoined the limit up to which it ought to be done, saying

headnotes.la: …m pervenerimus jam, nequaquam necesse est ut solemnem Domino de nostra lamentatione faciamus. Anima ergo, quae jam per amorem compungi desiderat, quae jam contemplari visione sponsi sui appetit, dicat
headnotes.en: … to the Lord out of our lamentation. Let the soul, therefore, which already desires to be pricked with compunction through love, which already seeks to contemplate in the vision of her bridegroom, say

headnotes.la: Vel certe osculum oris ejus est ipsa perfectio pacis internae, ad quam cum pervenerimus nihil remanebit amplius quod quaeramus. Unde et apte subjungitur
headnotes.en: Or assuredly the kiss of his mouth is that very perfection of inward peace, at which when we have arrived nothing further will remain that we should seek. Whence also it is aptly subjoined

headnotes.la: Vinum est scientia Dei, quam in ista vita positi accipimus. Ubera autem sponsi tunc amplectimur, cum eum in aeterna patria jam per amplexum praesentiam contemplamur. Dicat ergo
headnotes.en: …f God, which, placed in this life, we receive. But we embrace the breasts of the bridegroom then, when in the eternal fatherland we contemplate him, now present, through embrace. Let her say therefore

headnotes.la: …ntulisti, magnum est vinum notitiae tuae quo me inebrias, sed ubera tua vino meliora sunt, quia tunc per speciem et per sublimitatem contemplationis transcenditur, quidquid de te modo per fidem scitur
headnotes.en: … wherewith thou inebriatest me; but thy breasts are better than wine, because then, through sight and through the sublimity of contemplation, whatever is now known of thee through faith is transcended

headnotes.la: …ta, dum in virtute scientiae, virtute castitatis, virtute misericordiae, virtute humilitatis, virtute charitatis pollet. Si sanctorum vita odorem aromatum ex virtutibus non haberet, Paulus non diceret
headnotes.en: … the virtue of chastity, the virtue of mercy, the virtue of humility, the virtue of charity. If the life of the saints did not have the odor of aromatical spices out of the virtues, Paul would not say

headnotes.la: … odor unguentorum Dei aromatibus virtutum nostrarum. Et si jam magna sunt quae accepimus, valde tamen potiora sunt, quae de contemplatione Creatoris nostri accepturi sumus. Unde anhelet anima et dicat
headnotes.en: …es of our virtues. And if the things we have received are already great, yet far more powerful are those which we are to receive from the contemplation of our Creator. Whence let the soul pant and say

headnotes.la: …d est invisibilis, se visibilem reddidit. Si enim non se effunderet, nequaquam nobis innotesceret. Effundit se unguentum, cum se et dominum servavit, et hominem exhibuit. De qua effusione Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: … For if he had not poured himself out, he would by no means have become known to us. The ointment pours itself out when he both kept himself Lord and showed himself man. Of which pouring out Paul says

headnotes.la: Quod Paulus dixit,
headnotes.en: What Paul said,

headnotes.la: hoc Salomon dixit
headnotes.en: this Solomon said,

headnotes.la: …innotuit, dicatur ei: Unguentum effusum nomen tuum. Sed quia in Hebraica veritate aliquid aliter habetur, compellimur ad superiora apostropham facere, et nonnulla aliter inserere. Denique cum dixisset
headnotes.en: …t is thy name. But because in the Hebrew verity something is otherwise held, we are compelled to make an apostrophe to the things above, and to insert some things otherwise. Finally, when she had said

headnotes.la: et subjunxit
headnotes.en: and had subjoined

headnotes.la: …quorumdam rursus iterare. Vinum, inquiunt, erat verbum nuntiatorum, delatum per angelos, qui ad prophetas vel in prophetis loquebantur, sicut ait Zacharias propheta [n: (Cap. II)]. Et dixit ad Angelum
headnotes.en: …in men. The wine, they say, was the word of the messengers, brought down by angels, who spoke to the prophets or in the prophets, as Zacharias the prophet says [n: (Cap. II)]. And he said to the Angel

headnotes.la: … corporis Christi, et pinguissimum butyrum, sacri charismatis oleum, per quod Spiritus sanctus infunditur. De qua pinguedine, Ecclesia in alio Propheta deprecatur animae suae medullas repleri, dicendo
headnotes.en: …, and the richest butter, the oil of the sacred chrism, through which the Holy Spirit is poured in. Of which fatness the Church, in another Prophet, prays that the marrow of her soul be filled, saying

headnotes.la: Cujus odor sauciatas a peccatis animas resuscitat, cujus virtute pinguedinis in praedictis uberibus absconsam flagrantiam, quae post oscula suscepta collaudare sequenti docetur versiculo, dicens
headnotes.en: … again souls wounded by sins; by the power of whose fatness the fragrance hidden in the aforesaid breasts, which after the kisses received she is taught to praise in the following little verse, saying

headnotes.la: …acerdotes constituat, et ejus odor notitiae a solis ortu usque ad occasum omnem mundum impleverit. Quae intra se quam aliam flagrantiam potest intelligi continere, nisi Christi nomen? De quo sequitur,
headnotes.en: …wledge of it has filled the whole world from the rising of the sun even to its setting. What other fragrance can it be understood to contain within itself, save the name of Christ? Of which it follows

headnotes.la: …icut enim intra multitudinem cadaverum putridorum reclusi homines, morbo periclitantur, ita habitatoribus hujus mundi evenerat per Adam, pluralem deorum numerum inducente diabolo ore serpentis dicendo
headnotes.en: … multitude of putrid corpses are endangered by disease, so it had befallen the inhabitants of this world through Adam, the devil bringing in a plural number of gods by the mouth of the serpent, saying

headnotes.la: …ore passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi omnis mundus unius veri Dei Christi nomine notitia impletus probatur, ut per omnes nationes gentium quotidie quasi odor unguenti, virtutum recurrit flagrantia,
headnotes.en: …proved to be filled with the knowledge of the name of the one true God, Christ, so that through all the nations of the Gentiles the fragrance of the virtues runs back daily like the scent of ointment,

headnotes.la: …fugantur daemonia, omnis aegritudo cadit, pellitur languor, in virtute hujus nominis invocati. Ecce quibus odoribus dilectio amorque Christi adolescentulas accendit animas, scilicet de quibus nunc ait
headnotes.en: …y sickness falls away, languor is driven off, in the power of this name invoked. Behold with what odors the love and affection of Christ kindles the young maidens' souls — of whom, namely, he now says

headnotes.la: His enim praelibatis, ad superiorem suavissimi sensum doctoris regrediamur. Nam sequitur
headnotes.en: These things having been tasted beforehand, let us return to the sense above of the most sweet doctor. For it follows

headnotes.la: …elligere et aliter possumus. Potest enim adolescentia ad infirmitatem referri. Juveniles quippe aetates sunt ordines angelorum qui nulla debilitate victi sunt, nulla infirmitate superati. Dicatur ergo
headnotes.en: …d otherwise. For adolescence can be referred to weakness. For the youthful ages are the orders of the angels, who have been conquered by no debility, overcome by no infirmity. Let it therefore be said

headnotes.la: … superata, sicut debet sequi non praevalet. Videt ergo aliud in se esse quo tendit, aliud in se esse quod non valet, et recte dicit, trahe me. Quasi volentem nec valentem se viderat Paulus cum diceret
headnotes.en: … that there is one thing in itself whither it strives, another thing in itself which it is not able to do, and rightly it says, draw me. Paul had seen himself as willing and yet not able, when he said

headnotes.la: et
headnotes.en: and

headnotes.la: Quia ergo est aliquid quod nos incitat, aliud quod gravat, dicamus
headnotes.en: Since therefore there is something which incites us, and another which weighs us down, let us say

headnotes.la: …veranter sequitur. Immobile enim erat cor ad sequendum Deum, et post eum ambulare nolebat, cum adventus Domini in mundo apparuit, et ab insensibili sua statione humanas mentes movit. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: …as immovable for the following of God, and was unwilling to walk after him, when the coming of the Lord appeared in the world and moved human minds from their insensible standing. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: His autem non motus, sed cursus dicitur, quia non sufficit ut sequamur, nisi etiam desiderando curramus. Quia vero neque currere sufficit, nisi etiam perfecte curratur, Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: …to these not motion but running is spoken of, because it is not enough that we follow, unless we also run by desiring. But because neither does it suffice to run, unless it be run perfectly, Paul says

headnotes.la: …im currunt, qui ejus judicia considerant, ejus voluntatem suae praeferunt, et pervenire ad eum sub digna operatione cum discretione contendunt. Hinc Propheta voluntatem Dei considerans, et sequens ait
headnotes.en: …God who consider his judgments, who prefer his will to their own, and who strive to come to him under worthy work with discretion. Hence the Prophet, considering the will of God and following it, says

headnotes.la: Hic Petro consilium danti dicitur
headnotes.en: Here it is said to Peter as he gives counsel

headnotes.la: Quia ergo perfectae animae summa cautela Dei judicia contuentur, et neque per torporem, neque per indiscretum fervorem praevenire praesumunt, bene dicitur
headnotes.en: …hind me, Satan"] Since therefore perfect souls behold the judgments of God with the utmost caution, and presume to run before them neither through torpor nor through indiscreet fervor, well is it said

headnotes.la: Tunc enim post Deum currimus, quando et amando sequimur, et timendo divina judicia praevenimus. Sequitur
headnotes.en: For then do we run after God, when we both follow by loving and, by fearing, anticipate the divine judgments. It follows

headnotes.la: …que ad inimicorum dilectionem extenditur. Omnis qui in Ecclesia positus, jam sublimia rimatur secreta, jam occulta judicia considerat, quasi in cubiculum intrabit. De porta domus istius dicebat quidam
headnotes.en: …emies. Everyone set in the Church who now searches out the high secrets, who now considers the hidden judgments, will enter as it were into the bedchamber. Of the gate of that house a certain one said

headnotes.la: De ascensu spei dicebat
headnotes.en: Of the ascent of hope he said

headnotes.la: De tricliniis latis domus istius dicitur
headnotes.en: Of the broad dining-halls of that house it is said

headnotes.la: In mandato lato, specialiter charitas designatur. De cubiculo regis loquebatur qui dicebat
headnotes.en: In the broad commandment charity is specially designated. Of the bedchamber of the king he was speaking who said

headnotes.la: Et alias
headnotes.en: And elsewhere

headnotes.la: …sia in membris suis perfectis, in sanctis doctoribus, in eis qui jam pleni et radicati sunt in mysteriis Dei, quasi ad sublimia secreta pervenit, et adhuc in ista vita posita, jam illa penetrat, dicit
headnotes.en: …ers, in her holy teachers, in those who are now full and rooted in the mysteries of God, has come as it were to the high secrets, and, still set in this life, already penetrates those things, she says

headnotes.la: …am pervenire, ut contemplentur secreta Dei in cordibus suis, et nos parvuli habeamus fiduciam, quod quandoque ad veniam, quandoque ad ejus gratiam veniamus. Unde et ex verbis adolescentularum subditur
headnotes.en: … of God in their hearts, let us little ones also have confidence that at some time we shall come to pardon, at some time to his grace. Whence also, from the words of the young maidens, it is subjoined

headnotes.la: … qui perfecti sunt ingreditur cubiculum regis, adolescentulae spem sibi exsultationis promittunt. Quia dum fortes ad sublimia contemplanda perveniunt, infirmi spem de venia peccatorum sumunt, ideo ait
headnotes.en: …he king, the young maidens promise themselves the hope of exultation. Because while the strong come to the contemplating of high things, the weak take hope of pardon for their sins, therefore she says

headnotes.la: …stoli et omnes praedicatores Ecclesiae: vinum, sicut et superius diximus, fuit in prophetis, vinum fuit in lege. Sed quia ampliora mandata data sunt per apostolos, quam data fuerant per prophetas, ait
headnotes.en: …hurch: the wine, as we also said above, was in the prophets, the wine was in the law. But because fuller commandments were given through the apostles than had been given through the prophets, she says

headnotes.la: Quia qui ista possunt implere quae in Novo Testamento mandata sunt, illi scientiam legis sine dubio transcendunt. Quod tamen intelligere et aliter possumus
headnotes.en: Because they who can fulfill those things which are commanded in the New Testament, they without doubt transcend the knowledge of the law. Yet this we can also understand otherwise

headnotes.la: …ntiae, ut sciant considerare dona doctrinae. Dona enim spiritualis gratiae quasi quaedam mamillae sunt in pectore, quae subtiliter occultis meatibus spiritualibus ministrant, et eos nutriunt. Ideo ait
headnotes.en: … to consider the gifts of doctrine. For the gifts of spiritual grace are like certain teats in the bosom, which subtly minister to spiritual men by hidden passages and nourish them. Therefore she says

headnotes.la: …a quam acceperunt non extolluntur super illos, qui de sapientia sua extolluntur et efferuntur. Plus est enim humiliter sapere quam superbe sapere. Neque enim vere sapere est, humiliter non sapere, ait
headnotes.en: …bove those who are lifted up and puffed up on account of their own wisdom. For it is more to be wise humbly than to be wise proudly. For neither is it truly to be wise, not to be wise humbly; she says

headnotes.la: Quia scientes considerare dona spiritualis gratiae, transcendunt eos qui scientiam quidem habent, sed cognitionem in memoria donorum non habent. Aperte ergo dicere est
headnotes.en: Because those who know how to consider the gifts of spiritual grace transcend those who indeed have knowledge, but have not in memory the knowing of the gifts. Openly, therefore, is it to say

headnotes.la: quia fortior humilitas est quam scientia. Vinum est scientia quae inebriat memoriam uberum, quae inebriat quem ad cognitionem donorum revocat. Dicat
headnotes.en: because humility is stronger than knowledge. Wine is the knowledge which inebriates the memory of the breasts, which inebriates him whom it calls back to the knowing of the gifts. Let her say

headnotes.la: …est. Vellet enim non esse quod timeret ut opera bona non faceret. Qui vero bona opera per amorem agit, et in opere et desiderio rectus est. Sed dulcedo amoris timentibus absconditur. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: … fears, so that he might not do good works. But he who does good works through love is upright both in work and in desire. But the sweetness of love is hidden from those who fear. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: …tio illius est, ut judicem venientem non timeat, ut quidquid de aeternis suppliciis audierit, non formidet. Unde et Paulus dum adventum judicis exspectaret, dum praemia aeternae vitae quaereret, dixit
headnotes.en: …ge when he comes, so that whatever he has heard of eternal punishments, he does not dread. Whence Paul also, while he awaited the coming of the judge, while he sought the rewards of eternal life, said

headnotes.la: …iderunt. Sed hi qui crediderunt, ab infidelibus despecti sunt et persecutionem passi, quasi in viam gentium discessisse judicati sunt. Unde Ecclesia in eisdem clamat adversum eos qui conversi non sunt
headnotes.en: …he unbelieving and suffered persecution, and were judged to have departed, as it were, into the way of the Gentiles. Whence the Church cries out in those same ones against those who were not converted

headnotes.la: Nigra quidem vero judicio, sed formosa per illustrationem gratiae. Quomodo nigra?
headnotes.en: Black indeed by a true judgment, but comely through the illumination of grace. How black?

headnotes.la: …t Cedar tabernacula Esau fuerunt. Quomodo ergo nigra? Sicut tabernacula Cedar. Quia in conspectu vestro ad similitudinem gentium judicata sum, id est ad similitudinem peccatorum. Quomodo ergo formosa?
headnotes.en: …of Cedar were Esau's. How then black? As the tabernacles of Cedar. Because in your sight I have been judged after the likeness of the Gentiles, that is, after the likeness of sinners. How then comely?

headnotes.la: … peccatorem invenit, in sole decoloratus invenitur. Sed ecce pars ista quae ex Judaea credidit, persecutionem ab infidelibus Judaeis passa est, afflicta multis tribulationibus ac pressa. Unde sequitur
headnotes.en: …Christ is found discolored in the sun. But behold, that part which believed out of Judea suffered persecution from the unbelieving Jews, afflicted with many tribulations and pressed. Whence it follows

headnotes.la: …fidelitate remanserunt, bellum persecutionis contra synagogae fideles gesserunt. Sed dum persecutionem patitur ea pars quae ex Judaea venit ad fidem, discessit ad praedicationem gentium. Unde sequitur
headnotes.en: … war of persecution against the faithful of the synagogue. But while that part which came out of Judea to the faith suffers persecution, it departed to the preaching of the Gentiles. Whence it follows

headnotes.la: Quia, dum me persequuntur qui in Judaea sunt, in ecclesiis me custodem fecerunt
headnotes.en: Because, while those who are in Judea persecute me, they have made me a keeper in the churches

headnotes.la: quia Judaeam deserui. Unde et Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: because I forsook Judea. Whence Paul also says

headnotes.la: …ustodire voluimus, sed quia nos ipsi respuistis ad alienarum nos vinearum custodiam transmittitis. Ista quae de Synagoga diximus ad fidem conversa, dicamus modo de Ecclesia ex gentibus ad fidem vocata
headnotes.en: … you send us over to the keeping of other men's vineyards. These things which we have said of the Synagogue converted to the faith, let us now say of the Church called out of the Gentiles to the faith

headnotes.la: … vocat. Hierusalem quippe *visio pacis* dicitur. Considerat quid fuit, considerat quid facta est, et confitetur praeteritas culpas ne superba sit. Confitetur praesentem vitam, ne ingrata sit, et dicit
headnotes.en: … vision of peace.* She considers what she was, considers what she has become, and confesses her past faults, that she be not proud. She confesses her present life, that she be not ungrateful, and says

headnotes.la: …ra per vitam praeteritam, formosa per conversationem sequentem. Quomodo nigra? Sicut tabernacula Cedar. Cedar quippe tabernacula gentium fuerunt, tabernacula tenebrarum fuerunt. Et gentibus dictum est
headnotes.en: … of life that follows. How black? As the tabernacles of Cedar. For the tabernacles of Cedar were the tabernacles of the Gentiles, they were the tabernacles of darkness. And to the Gentiles it was said

headnotes.la: …quia mortificata caro fiunt. Sed ecce erant in Judaea fideles, qui dedignabantur venire ad fidem gentilium. Unde et Petrum redarguunt, quod Cornelium susceperat. Unde et hic Ecclesia gentium subjungit
headnotes.en: …old, there were faithful in Judea who disdained to come to the faith of the Gentiles. Whence they rebuke Peter also, that he had received Cornelius. Whence here too the Church of the Gentiles subjoins

headnotes.la: Nolite despicere gentilitatem infidelitatis meae, nolite despicere peccata priora, nolite attendere quod fui. Quare?
headnotes.en: Do not despise the heathenism of my unbelief, do not despise my former sins, do not regard what I was. Why?

headnotes.la: …lem superna est. Ipsi pugnaverunt contra Ecclesiam, dum ab infidelitate in fide praedicationis suae, quasi quibusdam lanceis confoderunt. Unde et Paulus quasi quidam pugnator dicit [n: (II Thess. II)]
headnotes.en: …They fought against the Church, when out of unbelief, in the faith of their preaching, they pierced her through as with certain lances. Whence Paul also, as a certain fighter, says [n: (II Thess. II)]

headnotes.la: Qui altitudinem destruit utique pugnator est; isti ergo pugnatores, isti filii matris Hierusalem debellaverunt Ecclesiam ab errore suo, ut illam fundarent ad justitiam
headnotes.en: …gitationum*] He who destroys height is assuredly a fighter; these fighters, therefore, these sons of the mother Jerusalem, warred down the Church from her error, that they might found her unto justice

headnotes.la: Et quid fecerunt pugnantes?
headnotes.en: And what did they do in fighting?

headnotes.la: …gnant in me vitia, quasi mala mea in me expugnant. Fructificationem et virtutum studia mihi dederunt, in vineis me custodem fecerunt, ut fructificationem afferrem. Post expugnationem specialiter dicat
headnotes.en: …y own evils within me. They gave me fruitfulness and the pursuits of the virtues; they made me keeper in the vineyards, that I might bring forth fruitfulness. After the storming, let her say specially

headnotes.la: … sunt, sed quod fuerunt. Sani vero doctores et confitentur quod fuerunt, et proferunt quod sunt, ut nec peccatores esse abscondant, nec iterum dona velut ingrati denegent. Dicat ergo in istis Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …ers both confess what they were and bring forward what they are, so that they neither hide that they were sinners, nor again, like ungrateful men, deny the gifts. Let the Church therefore say in these

headnotes.la: Nigra per me, formosa per donum. Nigra de praeterito, formosa ex eo facta sum in futuris. Quomodo nigra? quomodo formosa? Nigra
headnotes.en: Black through myself, comely through the gift. Black from the past; comely, from that I have been made so in things to come. How black? how comely? Black

headnotes.la: Et non est justum ut aliquis ex praeterita vita pensetur, et non magis attendatur quod fuit, sed quod est. Unde subjungit
headnotes.en: And it is not just that anyone be weighed from his past life, and that there be not more regarded what he was, but what he is. Whence she subjoins

headnotes.la: …itur nimius aestus terrenorum desideriorum. Unde ergo fusca? Quia decoloravit me sol. Ita intelligitur: Nolite considerare quod nigra fui antea per infidelitatem, quia sol Christus de quo scriptum est
headnotes.en: …earthly desires. Whence then brown? Because the sun hath discolored me. Thus it is understood: Do not consider that I was black before through unbelief, because the sun, Christ — of whom it is written

headnotes.la: decoloravit me per fidem
headnotes.en: — has discolored me through faith

headnotes.la: …uod rationales conditi simus, quasi quamdam societatem fraternitatis habemus, quia angeli ab eadem potentia conditi sunt qua et nos. Quia tamen cadentes angeli quotidie contra nos bellum gerunt, dicit
headnotes.en: …tional, have as it were a certain fellowship of brotherhood, because the angels were founded by the same power by which we also were. Yet because the falling angels daily wage war against us, she says

headnotes.la: Ecce dum pugnant isti spiritus rationes, spiritus isti filii matris dum pugnant contra animam faciunt eam terrenis rebus incumbere, actionibus saeculi vacare, res transitorias quaerere. Unde subjungit
headnotes.en: …ht — these spirits, the sons of the mother, while they fight against the soul, make it lean upon earthly things, be at leisure for the actions of the world, seek transitory things. Whence she subjoins

headnotes.la: …se considerant quod juxta ipsos est, non ex eo quod sunt. Juxta ipsos sunt dignitates, juxta ipsos interiora ministeria. Et dum custodiunt quod juxta se habent, seipsos custodire negligunt. Dicat ergo
headnotes.en: …m, not from that which they are. Beside them are dignities, beside them are the inner ministries. And while they keep what they have beside them, they neglect to keep themselves. Let her say therefore

headnotes.la: In meridie sol ferventior est; omnis qui in fide fervet, in amore fervet. Iste sponsus qui subter hinnulus vocatur, in corde ipsorum pascit virtutum viriditate, ait
headnotes.en: At midday the sun is more fervent; everyone who is fervent in faith is fervent in love. This bridegroom, who below is called a fawn, feeds in their heart with the greenness of virtues; she says

headnotes.la: Quare sic quaerat ubi pascat, ubi cubet, causam reddidit inquisitionis suae
headnotes.en: Why she thus asks where he feeds, where he lies, she has given the cause of her inquiry

headnotes.la: …na suaderet, sodales quidem videbantur, sed inimici exstiterunt. Dum doctor esset Arius, Sabellius, Montanus, quasi sodales videbantur, sed dum districte discussi sunt, inimici apparuerunt. Dicat ergo
headnotes.en: …ed companions, but proved enemies. While Arius, Sabellius, Montanus was a teacher, they seemed as it were companions; but when they were strictly examined, they appeared enemies. Let her say therefore

headnotes.la: …tenere, considerant vitam sacerdotum qui eis praepositi sunt, et dum bene ipsi sacerdotes non vivunt, hi qui sequuntur, in errorem dilabuntur. Unde Ecclesia quasi in eisdem parvulis et fidelibus dicit
headnotes.en: …he priests who are set over them, and while those priests themselves do not live well, those who follow slip away into error. Whence the Church, as it were in those same little ones and faithful, says

headnotes.la: … cognovit quia ad imaginem Dei factus est. Si ad imaginem Dei factus est, non debet similitudinem jumentorum sequi, sive in luxuria, sive in appetitu praesenti devolvi. De qua ignorantia alibi dicitur
headnotes.en: … image of God. If he was made to the image of God, he ought not to follow the likeness of beasts, nor to be rolled down either in luxury or in present appetite. Of which ignorance it is said elsewhere

headnotes.la: Vestigia gregum sunt actiones populorum. Quae quanto multae sunt, tanto impeditae, tanto perversae. Dicatur ergo Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The steps of the flocks are the actions of the peoples. Which, by how much they are many, by so much are they hindered, by so much perverse. Let it therefore be said to the Church

headnotes.la: …est hoc ipsum quod ad imaginem meam facta es ignoras, egredere, foras exi. Si vero non cognoscis, aliquid facta es, egredere et abi post vestigia gregum. Sequere non exempla mea, sed exempla populorum
headnotes.en: …t made to my image, go forth, go outside. But if thou knowest not, thou hast been made something, go forth and go after the steps of the flocks. Follow not my examples, but the examples of the peoples

headnotes.la: Haedi nostri sunt motus carnales, haedi sunt nostrae tentationes illicitae
headnotes.en: Our kids are carnal motions; the kids are our unlawful temptations

headnotes.la: id est discede post exempla populorum
headnotes.en: that is, depart after the examples of the peoples

headnotes.la: …n humilitate, in castitate, in doctrina, in charitate fervet jam equus effectus est Creatoris nostri, jam in curru Dei positus est, jam sessorem Deum habet. Unde cuidam cui Dominus praesidebat dicitur
headnotes.en: …n doctrine, in charity has already been made a horse of our Creator, is already set in the chariot of God, already has God for his rider. Whence to a certain one over whom the Lord presided it is said

headnotes.la: Ac si diceret: Meus equus es, jam calces contra me jactare non potes, jam tibi ego praesideo. De istis equis alibi dicitur
headnotes.en: As if he should say: Thou art my horse; now thou canst not fling thy heels against me; now I preside over thee. Of these horses it is said elsewhere

headnotes.la: Habet ergo currum Deus, quia animabus sanctis praesidet, et per animas sanctas circumquaque discurrit. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: … madest a way in the sea for thy horses, in the mud of many waters"] God therefore has a chariot, because he presides over holy souls and runs about everywhere through holy souls. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: et reliqua. Habet tamen currus Pharao, qui tamen currus in mari Rubro submersi sunt. Dicit ergo sponsus
headnotes.en: and the rest. Pharaoh nevertheless has chariots, which chariots nevertheless were sunk in the Red Sea. The bridegroom therefore says

headnotes.la: …nis per reprobam vitam quae sequitur eos: ita et per pietatem multi qui equi Pharaonis esse videntur, per sanctam vitam quam in fine suo servaturi sunt, equis Dei assimilantur. Unde blanditur et dicit
headnotes.en: …ows them, so also through piety many who seem to be horses of Pharaoh are, through the holy life which they will keep at their end, likened to the horses of God. Whence he speaks flatteringly and says

headnotes.la: …iorum munitus, gladiis divinarum Scripturarum accinctus, spiculis sententiarum ornatus, defendere possis: qui semper non corpora, sed animas fidelium exstinguere quaerunt. Unde Petrus hortatur, dicens
headnotes.en: … Church among your subjects from the shields, that is to say, of the inward malignant spirits: who always seek to extinguish not the bodies, but the souls of the faithful. Whence Peter exhorts, saying

headnotes.la: …re vestra nobilitas docte valeat, hujus voluminis, aliorumque librorum expositionibus studere congruis post dispositionem imperii horis satagas, ut merito dicere gratulabunda queat, quod istic legitur
headnotes.en: …rs, be busy to study the expositions of this volume and of other books at fitting hours after the ordering of the empire, so that she may deservedly and with rejoicing be able to say what is read here

headnotes.la: Et illud
headnotes.en: And that

headnotes.la: …ri jam nunquam alia societur, sed in omni vita proprium conjugem amissum desiderando requirit. Cui per castitatis et verecundiae decorem, Ecclesia in genarum pulchritudine congrue comparatur. Ait enim
headnotes.en: …other, but in all its life it seeks by longing its own lost mate. To which, through the comeliness of chastity and of modesty, the Church is fittingly compared in the beauty of her cheeks. For he says

headnotes.la: …a sunt, sed secundum opinionem aliquorum praecelsior sensus in hac comparatione latere dicitur. Nam quibusdam videtur illius turturis pulchritudinis genas Ecclesiae comparari, de qua in Psalmo dicitur
headnotes.en: …nion of some, a loftier sense is said to lie hid in this comparison. For to certain men it seems that the cheeks of the Church's beauty are compared to that turtledove of which it is said in the Psalm

headnotes.la: …ssima vita vel fama cernitur. Et quia sancta Ecclesia in suis praesulibus et doctoribus castitate et varietate virtutum, turturis, id est Christi imaginem imitatur, necessario ab ipso laudatur dicendo
headnotes.en: …iscerned. And because holy Church in her prelates and teachers imitates by chastity and by variety of virtues the image of the turtledove, that is, of Christ, she is necessarily praised by him, saying

headnotes.la: Sequitur
headnotes.en: It follows

headnotes.la: …stamenti, quae murenulis aureis designatur, videlicet quia auro spiritualium sensuum fulget interius, et argento coelestis eloquii nitet exterius praedicant, recte in eis Ecclesia laudatur dum dicitur
headnotes.en: …den *murenulae* — namely, because it shines within with the gold of spiritual senses, and glitters without with the silver of heavenly eloquence — rightly is the Church praised in them when it is said

headnotes.la: vel catenulas
headnotes.en: or little chains

headnotes.la: …is situ redolente ut cypressum, aspero sapore, folio parvo, densoque; cujus cacumina in aristas se spargunt, ideoque gemina dote pigmentarii nardi spicas ac folia celebrant. Et hoc est quod ait Marcus
headnotes.en: …ith a small and dense leaf, whose tips spread themselves out into ears; and therefore the perfumers celebrate the spikes and the leaves of spikenard for a twofold endowment. And this is what Mark says

headnotes.la: …, sed omnia herbae, praeter Indicum quod pretiosius est. Mystice autem devotio haec Mariae Domino ministrantis fidem ac pietatem designat Ecclesiae sanctae, quae loquitur hic in amoris cantico, dicens
headnotes.en: …except the Indian, which is more precious. But mystically this devotion of Mary ministering to the Lord designates the faith and the piety of holy Church, which speaks here in the song of love, saying

headnotes.la: …us Mariae complevit, et quotidie in omnibus suis membris spiritualiter implere non desinit. Quae totum diffusa per orbem gloriantur, et dicunt: Deo autem gratias qui semper triumphat nos in omni loco,
headnotes.en: …of Mary, and does not cease daily to fulfill spiritually in all her members. Which, spread through the whole world, glory and say: But thanks be to God, who always maketh us to triumph in every place,

headnotes.la: …Simonis leprosi. Nardus vero ipsae mulieres quae primo diluculo ad monumentum cum aromatibus venerunt, ut ungerent Christum, et famam illius resurrectionis credentibus divulgarent. Unde eis dictum est
headnotes.en: … But the spikenard is the women themselves who came at first dawn to the tomb with spices, to anoint Christ and to spread abroad to believers the report of his resurrection. Whence it was said to them

headnotes.la: Seu accubitus Christi beatitudo est secreti coelestis. Ait enim
headnotes.en: … Galilee, there they shall see me"; the clause *praecedit vos in Galilaeam, ibi eum videbitis* stands at Matth. XXVIII, 7] Or the repose of Christ is the beatitude of the heavenly secret. For she says

headnotes.la: …orum in Ecclesia, magnae nobis gratiam suavitatis administrant. Vel etiam accubitus regis sancta electorum intelligitur Ecclesia. In ea Christus requiem sibi invenit, sicut per Prophetam ipse loquitur
headnotes.en: …inister to us the grace of great sweetness. Or also the repose of the king is understood as the holy Church of the elect. In her Christ found rest for himself, as he himself speaks through the Prophet

headnotes.la: Nardus Ecclesiae dicitur propter odorem virtutum. Unde Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: The spikenard is said of the Church on account of the odor of the virtues. Whence the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …em perpendit passum in amaritudine suae passionis. Unde semper habens in memoria recordationis quam propinqua est uberibus pectoris, et qualiter passus est pro ipsa in gloriam suae redemptionis, dicit
headnotes.en: …in the bitterness of his passion. Whence, always having in the memory of recollection how near he is to the breasts of the bosom, and how he suffered for her unto the glory of her redemption, she says

headnotes.la: Bene ait
headnotes.en: Well does he say

headnotes.la: …cet Christus ex Judaeis secundum carnem genitus, atque ab ipsis in lignum crucis velut botrus suspensus, sed tertia die post torcular mortis, laetitiam resurrectionis suis ostendit discipulis. Et bene
headnotes.en: …according to the flesh, and hung by them upon the wood of the cross like a cluster, yet on the third day after the winepress of death showed the gladness of the resurrection to his disciples. And well

headnotes.la: …onis Christi imitari desiderat, ut ad gloriam resurrectionis cum Christo perveniat et non cum haedis ad sinistram, sed cum ovibus segregari mereatur ad dexteram, dicamus plenius. Denique cum dixisset,
headnotes.en: … come with Christ to the glory of the resurrection, and may deserve to be set apart not with the kids on the left, but with the sheep on the right, let us speak more fully. Finally, when she had said,

headnotes.la: addidit mihi: intellexit pro sua salute fuisse passum, suaque pro gloria resurrexisse a mortuis. Ait namque
headnotes.en: she added to me: she understood that he had suffered for her salvation, and had risen from the dead for her glory. For she says

headnotes.la: …as, improperia, pericula, naufragia, imbres lapidum, praecipitationem profundi, variarumque poenarum aculeos et alia multa. Cum haec susceperit propter mortem sui Redemptoris, cum magna laetitia dicit
headnotes.en: …rs of stones, the headlong casting into the deep, and the stings of various punishments, and many other things. When she has undergone these for the death of her Redeemer, with great gladness she says

headnotes.la: …re expellendos. Tunc jam mundus et cum orationibus paratus, hospitium divinum est, ut ipsum jam tam magna fiducia Christum invitet in cordis sui recessum, tanquam intra ubera sua dicentem in Evangelio
headnotes.en: …and made ready with prayers, she is a divine lodging, so that now with such great confidence she invites Christ himself into the recess of her heart, as though within her breasts, saying in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Seu etiam in ubera sua Ecclesia commorari laetatur, inter illos procul dubio viros qui pro aetate, vel pro possibilitate lacte doctrinae suae spirituali parvulos nutriunt. De quibus ipse Dominus dicit
headnotes.en: …ween her breasts, among those men without doubt who, according to their age or according to their capacity, nourish little ones with the spiritual milk of their teaching. Of whom the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: …uper terram de omni re quamcumque petierint fiet illis a Patre meo*, "if two of you shall consent upon earth, concerning anything whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done to them by my Father"] And

headnotes.la: Quorum unus ex uberibus suis auditoribus dicebat
headnotes.en: One of whom said out of his own breasts to his hearers

headnotes.la: …duo Testamenta ubera sunt Ecclesiae. Quorum in medio Christus commoratur. Et quia legislator Moyses, et eximius prophetarum Elias, sermocinantes fuerunt de excessu passionis illius, propterea sequitur
headnotes.en: …reasts of the Church. In whose midst Christ abides. And because Moses the lawgiver, and Elias the chief of the prophets, were the ones speaking of the departure of his passion, therefore there follows

headnotes.la: …s haedi.* Est ergo botrus Cypri amicae suae Ecclesiae, dum peccatoribus tristitiam, vel moerorem poenitentiae in mentibus seminat, ut eos ad illam beatitudinem sublimet, de qua ipse in Evangelio dixit
headnotes.en: … of Cyprus to his friend the Church, while he sows in the minds of sinners the sadness, or the mourning, of penance, that he may lift them up to that blessedness of which he himself said in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …rum, in nulla secta philosophorum, in nulla adulatione schismaticorum, ubi si transplantatus fuerit aliquis, deceptus perversitatis suae fama, deperit arefactus. Haec profecto intelligens Ecclesia ait
headnotes.en: …of philosophers, in no flattery of schismatics, where, if anyone be transplanted, deceived by the report of his own perversity, he perishes withered. Understanding these things indeed, the Church says

headnotes.la: …succensa in ejus amore, laudat ejus pulchritudinem. Non potest aliquis cujuspiam quem diligit minime, decorem laudare, nec potest eum cujus moribus non concordat diligere, sicut Apostolus docet dicens
headnotes.en: … kindled in his love, she praises his beauty. No one can praise the comeliness of anyone whom he loves not at all, nor can he love him with whose ways he does not agree, as the Apostle teaches, saying

headnotes.la: … videre potest et laudando extollere, qui sanctis operibus spiritum ejus in sua retinuerit mente, ideoque praesenti loco, Ecclesia plena spiritu veritatis, sicut ipse sponsus superius ostendit, dicens
headnotes.en: …extol it with praise, who by holy works has kept his Spirit in his own mind; and therefore in the present place, the Church, full of the Spirit of truth, as the bridegroom himself showed above, saying

headnotes.la: …in Jordane de coelo super assumptum hominem descendit, et pulchritudinem corporis ejus sine peccato, et decorem verae animae sine mendacio et dolo agnoscens, reciproca geminataque effert laude dicendo
headnotes.en: …aven upon the assumed man in the Jordan — and recognizing the beauty of his body without sin, and the comeliness of his true soul without lie and guile, utters in reciprocal and doubled praise, saying

headnotes.la: …i sub vocabulo lectuli Filii Dei et Ecclesiae conjunctio celebrata, ubi cum eo Ecclesia delectabilem somnum passionis et gaudium aeternae vigilationis meruit invenire, clamante Apostolo ad ejus membra
headnotes.en: …on of God and of the Church was celebrated; where with him the Church deserved to find the delightful sleep of the passion and the joy of the eternal waking, while the Apostle cries out to her members

headnotes.la: … superiorem sensum exsequamur. Sepulcrum Domini lectulum intelligimus, ubi caro ipsius per soporem mortis velut in lectulo quievit, quod vere floruit per gloriam resurrectionis. Ait enim divinus sermo
headnotes.en: …erstand the sepulchre of the Lord, where his flesh, through the slumber of death, rested as though in a little bed, which truly flowered through the glory of the resurrection. For the divine word says

headnotes.la: …in quibus Christus requiescit velut sub tecto. Et ut manifestius pateat, dicamus sub exemplo: Natura cedrorum semper crescere fertur, nec aliquando sinitur ire in senectam, secundum illud Psalmographi
headnotes.en: …, that it may lie open more plainly, let us speak by an example: The nature of the cedars is said always to grow, nor is it ever suffered to pass into old age, according to that saying of the Psalmist

headnotes.la: …t, mundum videlicet gentilium vel haereticorum, qui ipsam impugnant, et ne otio torpescat, contra hostes armari impugnarique permittitur, ut post pugnam ejus fortitudo appareat. De talibus Dominus ait
headnotes.en: … heretics, who assail her; and lest she grow numb with idleness, she is permitted to be armed against enemies and to be assailed, so that after the fight her strength may appear. Of such the Lord says

headnotes.la: quod est doctrina haereticorum. Et apostolus [n: (I Cor. VI)]
headnotes.en: which is the teaching of the heretics. [var: Vulg. *a fermento Pharisaeorum et Sadducaeorum*, "of the Pharisees and Sadducees"] And the Apostle [n: (I Cor. VI)]

headnotes.la: Aut qui est sensus templo Dei cum idolis? Aut quae communicatio Christi cum Belial? Et prope similiter Isaias ait
headnotes.en: … what communication hath Christ with Belial? [var: Vulg. II Cor. VI, 16 *qui consensus templo Dei cum idolis*, "what agreement hath the temple of God with idols"] And nearly in like manner Isaias says

headnotes.la: Quod autem dicit
headnotes.en: …Isa. LII, 11 *exite de medio eius … mundamini qui fertis vasa Domini*, "go out from the midst of her"; *de medio eorum*, "from the midst of them", is the reading of II Cor. VI, 17] But in that he says

headnotes.la: …obatur. Ac si Ecclesiae dicatur: Tu requiem quaeris, sed laudem lectuli recordare, quod candidior tribulationum aculeis efficieris, et majores fructus praedicationis quam quietis acquires. Et bene ait
headnotes.en: …u seekest rest, but remember the praise of the little bed, that thou art made whiter by the goads of tribulations, and shalt acquire greater fruits from preaching than from quiet. And well does he say

headnotes.la: Sicut igitur ante incarnationis mysterium
headnotes.en: As therefore before the mystery of the incarnation,

headnotes.la: secundum Apostolum,
headnotes.en: according to the Apostle,

headnotes.la: …lsione usque ad Virginis partum multis laboribus et intolerabilibus daemonum impugnationibus affecta est humana progenies, quae hic sub Ecclesiae persona amica est appellata, in ejus adventu qui dixit
headnotes.en: …man offspring was afflicted with many labors and with intolerable assaults of the demons — which offspring is here, under the person of the Church, called the friend; and at the coming of him who said

headnotes.la: sub tegmine defensionis ejus, credendo unum Deum, requiescens laeta dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *et ego reficiam vos*, "and I will refresh you"] resting under the covering of his protection, believing in one God, she says with gladness

headnotes.la: Quam dulcedinem regni coelorum quanquam praesens protectio possit intelligi, et beatorum requiem nominat, sive corpus ejus, et sanguinem delibando, vitam aeternam conferentem, exsultans ait
headnotes.en: …dom of the heavens — although present protection may be understood, and she names the rest of the blessed — or else, tasting his body and his blood, which confer eternal life, she says with exultation

headnotes.la: Licet ut dulcedo divinarum Scripturarum intelligatur in praedicatoribus sanctis, qui guttura Domini appellantur, prolata sit. De qua dulcedine ait Propheta
headnotes.en: It may be that it was uttered so that the sweetness of the divine Scriptures should be understood in the holy preachers, who are called the throats of the Lord. Of which sweetness the Prophet says

headnotes.la: Et illud
headnotes.en: And that

headnotes.la: … Ecclesiae infundi monstratur, et sic per singulos gradus profectuum introducitur ad arcanam intelligentiam legis divinae, ut agnoscere possit omnia illa quae in Veteri Testamento sunt gesta. Ait enim
headnotes.en: …gh the several degrees of advancement she is led in to the hidden understanding of the divine law, that she may be able to recognize all those things which were done in the Old Testament. For she says

headnotes.la: Ac si dicatur: Sicut malum visu, odore et gustu antecedit omnia ligna silvestria, ita Christus antecedit omnes sanctos qui filii Dei vocantur. De quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: As if it were said: As the apple goes before all the trees of the wood in sight, in fragrance and in taste, so Christ goes before all the saints who are called the sons of God. Of whom it is said

headnotes.la: … Sub cujus umbra omni aestu tristitiae, omnique pondere peccati abjecto, Ecclesia multo tempore desideratam requiem inventam, et dulcissimo fructu saginata adolescentibus animabus adepta gaudia narrat
headnotes.en: …all the heat of sadness and all the weight of sin being cast off, the Church tells of the rest long desired and now found, and, fattened with the sweetest fruit, of the joys obtained for growing souls

headnotes.la: …t nonnulli opinantur, in cujus unitate Spiritus sanctus tantummodo dari solet et accipi. Cujus gratia hoc loco vini nomine designatur. Vinum, cum Spiritum sanctum accepissent apostoli, Judaei dixerunt
headnotes.en: …e unity alone the Holy Spirit is wont to be given and received. Whose grace is designated in this place by the name of wine. Wine — since, when the apostles had received the Holy Spirit, the Jews said

headnotes.la: …r, necessario cellam vinariam, scientiam et dulcedinem divinae legis vult intelligi. Ad quam dulcedinem invitat adolescentulas, et laudando festinare hortatur, quam Christus propinando docuit, cum ait
headnotes.en: …e and the sweetness of the divine law. To which sweetness she invites the young maidens, and by praising it urges them to hasten — the sweetness which Christ taught by giving it to drink, when he said

headnotes.la: In quo opere positos beatificat Propheta dicens
headnotes.en: …, "labor not for the meat which perisheth, but for that which endureth unto life everlasting" — the received text sets the negation on *cibum*] Those set in this work the Prophet calls blessed, saying

headnotes.la: …Filium in quo semper Pater, tertium Spitum sanctum, qui vera ratione de voce et verbo de Patre et Filio procedere comprobatur? qui per omnia Deus unus diligendus est, secundum illud in initio Decalogi
headnotes.en: …*], who by true reason is proved to proceed, as from voice and word, from the Father and the Son? Who through all is the one God to be loved, according to that saying at the beginning of the Decalogue

headnotes.la: Secundus ordo est,
headnotes.en: The second order is,

headnotes.la: Tertius ordo est,
headnotes.en: The third order is,

headnotes.la: …smetipsos. Iste est ordo charitatis. Ordinavit ergo Dei Filius in Ecclesia sua charitatem, ut sciat unusquisque Ecclesiae filius unicuique quo ordine charitatis impendat officium, dicendo in Evangelio
headnotes.en: …order of charity. The Son of God therefore has set charity in order in his Church, that every son of the Church may know in what order of charity he is to render his duty to each, saying in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Et per Apostolum ait
headnotes.en: And through the Apostle he says

headnotes.la: …tiam, quam cellam vinariam nominavit, introducuntur, sed qui parvum quantumcunque imitatus fuerit Paulum, qui dicebat [n: (II Cor. XI)]: Amplius om nibus laboravi, in vigiliis, in jejuniis, et caetera
headnotes.en: …d understanding which she named the wine cellar, but he who shall have imitated, however little, Paul, who said [n: (II Cor. XI)]: I have labored more than all, in watchings, in fastings, and the rest

headnotes.la: In capite hujus cantici in cubiculum, sive cellarium regis introducta Ecclesia laudat, ubi ingressa dicit,
headnotes.en: At the head of this canticle the Church, led into the bedchamber or the storeroom of the king, gives praise, where, having entered, she says,

headnotes.la: …e, et thesauri. Hic vero ad intelligendam divinam legem, et ad ordinem charitatis discendum se introductam dicit, non se laetari et exsultare, sed languere, eo quod, secundum Salomonem [n: (Eccle. I)]
headnotes.en: …he is led in to the understanding of the divine law and to the learning of the order of charity, and that she does not rejoice and exult, but languishes, for that, according to Solomon [n: (Eccle. I)]

headnotes.la: … cella scientiae legis, sed quia illum quem desiderat videre prout est adhuc non permittitur, aliorum exempla ad suam consolationem exposcit, quibus interim suum languorem temperare valeat. Ait namque
headnotes.en: …but because she is not yet permitted to see him whom she desires as he is, she demands the examples of others for her consolation, whereby she may be able meanwhile to temper her languor. For she says

headnotes.la: …ittitur, magna est consolatio si de aliorum profectibus laetetur, ut anima requiescat in bono opere proximi, quae adhuc contemplari non valet vultum Dei. Videamus qualis mens Pauli fuerat, qui dicebat
headnotes.en: …f she rejoice at the advances of others, so that the soul which is not yet able to contemplate the face of God may rest in the good work of her neighbor. Let us see what the mind of Paul was, who said

headnotes.la: Hinc est quod iterum dicit
headnotes.en: Hence it is that again he says

headnotes.la: Sed ecce qui dissolvi desideras, quo amore langueas videamus. Quia interim differri te conspicis fulciri, quaeso, floribus non requiris? Quaeris plane: nam sequitur
headnotes.en: …solved, let us see with what love thou languishest. Because meanwhile thou seest thyself put off, dost thou not seek, I pray, to be stayed up with flowers? Plainly thou dost seek it: for there follows

headnotes.la: Et proficientibus discipulis dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Phil. I, 24 *permanere autem in carne magis necessarium est propter vos*, "but to abide in the flesh is more needful for you"] And to his advancing disciples he says

headnotes.la: …pores, quasi inebriata laetitiae vino semper futurae beatitudinis, quamvis sponsum non cernat in praesenti, cur ad eam tarde perveniat dicit se amore languere. Illo procul dubio, de quo Propheta dicit
headnotes.en: … to come, although she does not discern the bridegroom in the present, says that she languishes with love, because she comes to him but slowly. With that love, without doubt, of which the Prophet says

headnotes.la: …. Habet ergo palatium Dominus noster Jesus Christus, quod intra se cellaria multa, et cellam vinariam, et camporum spatia continere intelligitur. Cujus flores beatus Paulus ingressus, admirando laudat
headnotes.en: …ist therefore has a palace, which is understood to contain within itself many storerooms, and a wine cellar, and the spaces of the fields. Whose flowers blessed Paul, having entered, praises in wonder

headnotes.la: …adjurantem filias Hierusalem, ne me in ejus amplexu quiescentem suscitarent. Vel vox illius evangelica est praedicatio. Et quid dicat vox ista dilecti Ecclesiae, in ipso Evangelio proprio ore declarat
headnotes.en: …not stir me up as I rested in his embrace. Or else his voice is the evangelical preaching. And what this voice of the beloved of the Church may say, he declares in the Gospel itself with his own mouth

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Matt. XXIV, 4 *videte ne quis vos seducat*, "take heed that no man seduce you"; *a pseudoprophetis*, "by false prophets", is not in the received text] And

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: …antur, quia nostrae salutis illustratio caecitatem cordis auferens in posteriore saeculi parte veniendo in carne se ostendit, quam Moysi petenti in monte Sina monstraverat. De quo mysterio David dicit
headnotes.en: …e blindness of the heart, showed itself by coming in the flesh in the latter part of the age — which illumination he had shown to Moses when he asked for it on Mount Sinai. Of which mystery David says

headnotes.la: …m nomine praenotantur, seu hinnulo cervorum propter humilitatis formam, necdum adhuc potentiae cornibus exaltatis, quibus in secundo adventu causaturus est mundum, de quibus dictum est in psalmo: Tunc
headnotes.en: …e harts on account of the form of his humility, the horns of his power not yet being lifted up, with which at the second coming he will plead against the world, of which it was said in the psalm: Then

headnotes.la: …m cervorum sine cornibus est, amorem in se potius visionis suae quam terribilitatem ostendit, sicut Dominus noster Christus in primo adventu fecisse dignoscitur. De cujus primo adventu mox subjungitur
headnotes.en: …without horns, and shows in itself the love of its own aspect rather than terribleness, as our Lord Christ is known to have done at his first coming. Of whose first coming there is presently subjoined

headnotes.la: … et humana pertulit, quasi per cancellos et fenestras ad homines venit ut Deus, ut appareret ex miraculis, sicut dictum est, et lateret ex passionibus, et homo cerneretur ex passionibus. Recte dicitur
headnotes.en: … were through lattices and windows: that as God he might appear from his miracles, as has been said, and lie hidden from his sufferings, and be discerned as man from his sufferings. Rightly is it said

headnotes.la: …continebat Ecclesiam, cum qua carne sepultus est, cum ipsa utique stat resurgens post parietem incredulitatis nostrae quem luteis operibus construxeramus peccando. De quibus dicit per Isaiam prophetam
headnotes.en: … whom he was buried in the flesh — with her indeed he stands, rising again, behind the wall of our unbelief, which we had built with muddy works by sinning. Of which he says through Isaias the prophet

headnotes.la: …uos compunctionem ad se convertendo prospiciat. Ubi vero venerimus ad veram conversionem baptismi praedicti vel poenitentiae, retollit eum de medio concessa venia peccatorum, et loquitur nobis dicendo
headnotes.en: …ction as we turn to him. But when we have come to the true conversion of the aforesaid baptism, or of penance, he takes it away out of the midst, pardon of sins being granted, and speaks to us, saying

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: Sicut et magister gentium, Paulus, docuit factum in ejus adventu
headnotes.en: Even as the master of the Gentiles, Paul, taught that it was done at his coming

headnotes.la: …a parietum septa propter persecutionis metum, post suam resurrectionem formidantibus et nimio terrore dejectis Apostolis, januis clausis ingressus, magnam fiduciam magnumque gaudium apportavit dicendo
headnotes.en: …or fear of persecution, after his resurrection, while the Apostles were afraid and cast down with exceeding terror, he entered, the doors being shut, and brought great confidence and great joy, saying

headnotes.la: Loquitur ei scilicet ad perfectionem vitae vocando, dicendo ei jam non timere mortis auctorem, diabolum, nec ultra residere intra incredulitatis et torporis claustra
headnotes.en: …peaks to her, that is, by calling her to the perfection of life, by telling her no longer to fear the author of death, the devil, nor to remain any longer within the barriers of unbelief and of torpor

headnotes.la: inquit,
headnotes.en: he says,

headnotes.la: …o vitam perditam reddidi. Modo jam non terrearis a morte, cui ego destruxi imperium. Stabat namque post parietem nostrum, quia nobis umbra sua obstabat sol justitiae, de quo propheta promiserat dicens
headnotes.en: …longer terrified by death, whose empire I have destroyed. For he was standing behind our wall, because the sun of justice stood in our way with his own shadow, of whom the prophet had promised, saying

headnotes.la: Qui loquitur Ecclesiae in apostolis, quando surgens a mortuis consolatur eos, dicens
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *timentibus nomen meum*, "that fear my name"] He speaks to the Church in the apostles when, rising from the dead, he consoles them, saying

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: Unde per hanc sententiam ad praedicationis officium provocatur, sicut ipsa dicit
headnotes.en: Whence by this saying she is summoned to the office of preaching, as she herself says

headnotes.la: id est ad praedicandum me hortatur dicens
headnotes.en: that is, he exhorts me to preach, saying

headnotes.la: …idamque asperitatem floridum verni adventus sui tempus ostendit, et quanta vel qualia gaudiorum esset praemia ei per suam praesentiam exhibiturus, futuram jam quasi factam narravit. Unde et ei dicitur
headnotes.en: …to how great and of what sort would be the rewards of joys that he was to display to her by his presence — has told what was still to come as though it were already done. Whence it is also said to her

headnotes.la: … fidei credentium flore decoravit. Eo tempore de quietis stratu ad officium praedicationis, imo de convalle lacrymarum ad paradisi Dei montem suae mortis exemplo Ecclesiam vocat. Denique cum dixisset,
headnotes.en: …alls the Church from the couch of repose to the office of preaching, nay rather from the valley of tears to the mountain of God's paradise, by the example of his own death. In short, when he had said,

headnotes.la: mox subjunxit,
headnotes.en: he presently added,

headnotes.la: …itiae Christo veniente, transit de hoc mundo ad tartara. Jam frigus infidelitatiis et imber iniquitatis recesserunt, quae totum orbem usque ad tempus Dominicae incarnationis et resurrectionis tegebant
headnotes.en: …sun of justice is come. Now the cold of unbelief [sic: *infidelitatiis*] and the rain of iniquity have departed, which covered the whole globe until the time of the Lord's incarnation and resurrection

headnotes.la: id est initia fidei et justitiae floruerunt in mundo crescente Ecclesia
headnotes.en: that is, the beginnings of faith and of justice flowered in the world as the Church grew

headnotes.la: …oris boni separantur a malis, ne vicinitate malorum depereant boni, ne perfidia incredulorum periclitentur credentes. Hoc utique tempus nuntiabatur venire putationis, de quo Dominus dicit in Evangelio
headnotes.en: …he nearness of the wicked the good perish, lest by the treachery of unbelievers believers be endangered. This, surely, was the time of pruning announced as coming, of which the Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …ontemplandum in sua substantia omnipotentem Deum ducimur, jam verborum guttae necessariae non erunt, ut pluvia debeat praedicationis infundi. Nam quod minus hic audire quis potest, ibi amplius videbit
headnotes.en: …od in his own substance, the drops of words will no longer be necessary, so that the rain of preaching should have to be poured out. For what a man can here hear less of, there he shall see more fully

headnotes.la: …eternae beatitudinis vita quaedam suavitatis primordia praegustare anima coeperit, quasi jam in floribus odoratur exiens, quod postquam egressa fuerit in fructu uberius habebit, unde et illuc subditur
headnotes.en: …the life of eternal blessedness, it is as though already going out it smells among the flowers what, after it has gone forth, it shall have more abundantly in the fruit; whence there also is subjoined

headnotes.la: …pus tunc adveniet, quando infructuosam ac noxiam corruptionis carnem deserimus. Qui fructus nobis erit uberrimus, visio unius Dei. Ut tempus putationis est, vocatio e mundo animae coelestium. Sequitur
headnotes.en: …flesh of corruption. Which fruit shall be for us most abundant: the vision of the one God. As is the time of pruning, so is the calling out of the world of the soul of the heavenly ones. There follows

headnotes.la: …amus opiniones diversorum, ne forte ignorasse causari videamur. Vocem turturis propter decorem castitatis beatam Mariam intelligi volunt, cujus vox primum audita est in terra nostra dicendo ad angelum
headnotes.en: …ead ignorance. The voice of the turtledove, on account of the comeliness of chastity, they would have understood as the blessed Mary, whose voice was first heard in our land when she said to the angel

headnotes.la: [n: (Luc. I.)] Et
headnotes.en: [n: (Luc. I.)] And

headnotes.la: . Et
headnotes.en: . And

headnotes.la: . Cui angelus respondit
headnotes.en: . To whom the angel answered

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: …sed etiam coelorum virtutes admirantes collaudant, per vitae ingressum enim, mortem fugatam, mundum reconciliatum gaudemus. Aliqui vero beatum Joannem Baptistam asserunt, cujus vox audita est dicentis
headnotes.en: …f the heavens praise in wonder; for through her the entrance of life, death put to flight, the world reconciled, are our joy. But some assert the blessed John the Baptist, whose voice was heard saying
