headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: …mnibus diebus vitae, cui semel fuerit conjuncta, desiderando requirit. Sed sciendum est, licet ita sit vox turturis quae audita est in terra nostra: illa est Domini Salvatoris, quae dicit in Evangelio
headnotes.en: … longing him to whom it was once joined. But it must be known that, although the voice of the turtledove which was heard in our land be such, it is that of the Lord and Saviour, who says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …onstricta nihil in se ficulnea, id est Synagoga, nisi amarissimum succum doctrinae quem animarum cibum mentitur, intelligitur habuisse. Sed in Domini adventu postquam turturis vox audita est dicentis,
headnotes.en: …erstood to have had in itself nothing but the most bitter juice of a teaching which it falsely gives out as food of souls. But at the Lord's coming, after the voice of the turtledove was heard saying,

headnotes.la: … liberata plebs, coepit, amotis malis doctoribus Pharisaeis, in Christo credendo florere, et suo exemplo aliarum gentium nationes ad florem credulitatis provocare. De quibus sequenti versiculo dicitur
headnotes.en: …ers, the Pharisees, being removed — to flower by believing in Christ, and by their own example to summon the nations of other peoples to the flower of belief. Of whom it is said in the following verse

headnotes.la: …us justitiae praedictarum nationum se exerat. Ac si ei dicatur: O sponsa et amica, cui tanta obtuli bona et pro qua tanta sustinui, surge et veni, accingere ad certamen, unde aeternam quietem accipias
headnotes.en: …aid to her: O bride and love, to whom I have offered such great goods and for whom I have borne such great things, arise and come, gird thyself for the contest, whence thou mayest receive eternal rest

headnotes.la: Quid sit petra Apostolus exponit
headnotes.en: What the rock is, the Apostle sets forth

headnotes.la: …uibus docetur anima ad gaudia regni coelorum venire. Potest foramen petrae intelligi, protectio ejusdem Domini Jesu Christi, ad quam confugit Ecclesia, velut columba ad foramen petrae. Hinc Isaias ait
headnotes.en: …f the kingdom of heaven. The hole of the rock may be understood as the protection of that same Lord Jesus Christ, to which the Church takes refuge, as a dove to the hole of the rock. Hence Isaias says

headnotes.la: …m malignorum spirituum Deum construxisse probatur. Nam sicut ipsi per Christum, ita et nos per apostolos agnoscentes divina mysteria, intra conspectum fidei quam ipsi confessi sunt continemur. Et quia
headnotes.en: …or as they [came to know] the divine mysteries through Christ, so we too, coming to know them through the apostles, are held within the sight of that faith which they themselves confessed. And because

headnotes.la: recte subjungitur
headnotes.en: it is rightly subjoined

headnotes.la: …atam. Sed calliditate insidiisque vulpium maturitatem fructus exspectantium ad demoliendam devorandamque parata, quae sunt perversarum animarum haereseos mordacissima dogmata ait Jesus suis doctoribus
headnotes.en: …lling down and devouring by the craft and the ambushes of the foxes that await the ripeness of the fruit — which are the most biting dogmas of the heresy of perverse souls — Jesus says to his teachers

headnotes.la: …quae nulla peccati nigredine sit maculata, non turpium verborum mendaciique absconsa, vel blasphemiarum raucedine voce horrida, sed dulcedinem suis laudibus resonantem reddit vicem, eadem Ecclesia ait
headnotes.en: …ckness of sin, not hidden by base words and by lying, nor dreadful of voice with the hoarseness of blasphemies, but she renders in turn a sweetness resounding in her praises; and that same Church says

headnotes.la: …us enim dilectus et adjutor Ecclesiae, nisi Christus, et nullus Christi dilectus, nisi Ecclesia: quia nullus alius recte diligit Christum, nisi unica Ecclesia, et nulla alia ab eo diligitur, nisi ipsa
headnotes.en: …here is no beloved and helper of the Church save Christ, and no beloved of Christ save the Church: because no other rightly loves Christ save the one only Church, and no other is loved by him save she

headnotes.la: …archarum genitus, qui post resurrectionem suam ad coelos remeans, superexaltatus est super montes Bethel, quae *domus Dei* dicitur, id est supernam patriam angelorum. Unde Psalmista ad eum loquens ait
headnotes.en: …ction returning to the heavens was exalted above the mountains of Bethel, which is called *the house of God*, that is, the heavenly fatherland of the angels. Whence the Psalmist, speaking to him, says

headnotes.la: …iete cordis Dominum suum cogitat. Quem quaerens ob hoc minime invenit, ut amore illius accensa ardentius quaerens. Per noctem quaerimus, quia et si jam mens in illo vigilet, tamen adhuc caligat oculus
headnotes.en: …seeking, she therefore finds not at all, in order that, kindled with love of him, seeking more ardently. By night we seek, because even if the mind already keeps watch in him, yet the eye is still dim

headnotes.la: … impendit quaerendo, qui aequalem hominibus absque peccato et coaeternam Patri, non fuerit utraque natura confessus Deum, qui redemit, et hominem per quem redemit perditos Deus, de quo Psalmista dicit
headnotes.en: …who has not confessed in both natures — equal to men without sin, and coeternal with the Father — God who redeemed, and the man through whom God redeemed those who were lost; of whom the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. CXXVI.)] Vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem, id est Ecclesiam, apostoli vel caeteri doctores sunt qui sollicitam gentilitatem cum veritatis indagine invenerunt. De quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. CXXVI.)] The watchmen who keep the city, that is, the Church, are the apostles or the other teachers, who found the anxious heathen world by the searching out of truth. Of whom it is said

headnotes.la: …ter homines, divinitate tamen super homines fuit. Quia nisi qui fidei passibus et pura mente omnes sanctos transierit, et Christum excellentiorem omnibus sanctis crediderit, invenire nequaquam poterit
headnotes.en: …ove men. For unless a man has passed by all the saints with the steps of faith and with a pure mind, and has believed Christ more excellent than all the saints, he will by no means be able to find him

headnotes.la: Teneo illum firma fide, donec in fine saeculi per officium praedicationis introducam illum in domum et in cubiculum Synagogae, quae me genuit in Domino,
headnotes.en: …house of my mother"] I hold him with firm faith, until at the end of the world, by the office of preaching, I bring him into the house and into the chamber of the Synagogue, which bore me in the Lord,

headnotes.la: …itus, subito ab infimis voluptatibus per desertum gentilitatis et idololatriae ad alta virtutum culmina et sponsi amplexus ascendisset. Vere desertus locus erat, ubi nomen Christi non fuerat nominatum
headnotes.en: …res, through the desert of heathenism and of idolatry, to the high summits of the virtues and to the embraces of the bridegroom. Truly it was a desert place where the name of Christ had not been named

headnotes.la: …m odor. Moraliter vero sancta electorum Ecclesia cum ab hoc mundo in sanctis precibus ardenti amore se erigit, per desertum quod deseruit ascendit. Fumus de incenso nascitur. Et per Psalmistam dicitur
headnotes.en: …ly Church of the elect raises herself from this world in holy prayers with burning love, she goes up through the desert which she has deserted. Smoke is born of incense. And by the Psalmist it is said

headnotes.la: …t, qui et carnem afficiunt, ne eis corruptionis vitia dominentur, et redolentem in conspectu Domini amoris sui hostiam incendunt, seque ipsos Deo in sanctis virtutibus exhibent. Unde et illic subditur
headnotes.en: …t the vices of corruption have dominion over them, and burn the fragrant victim of their love in the sight of the Lord, and show forth themselves to God in holy virtues. Whence there also is subjoined

headnotes.la: Columnae argenteae sunt doctores eloquii luce fulgentes
headnotes.en: The silver pillars are the teachers shining with the light of eloquence

headnotes.la: … mentem irradiat, ut per intentionem ibi requiescat, ubi praedicationis gratia non quaeratur. Sed adhuc quod clarum ostenditur intus, qualis sit ascensus adjungit, cum de eodem ferculo protinus subdit
headnotes.en: …t may rest there where the grace of preaching is not sought. But further, as to what is shown bright within, he adds of what sort the ascent is, when he immediately subjoins concerning the same litter

headnotes.la: …quippe charitatem, et ibi sine dubio praevenis, ubi et columna argentea erigitur, et ascensus purpureus tenetur: nam quia hoc propter nostram infirmitatem dicitur, aperte monstratur cum illic subditur
headnotes.en: …out doubt thou dost come beforehand, where both the silver pillar is raised and the purple going up is held: for that this is said on account of our weakness is openly shown when it is subjoined there

headnotes.la: …ecreta, non infirmae, sed perfectae animae convocantur, quae in rege Salomone dominium intelligunt, quibus dicitur: Egredimini mente et actu de turbulenta mundi conversatione, ut regem valeatis videre
headnotes.en: …souls are called together, they who understand dominion in king Solomon, to whom it is said: Go forth in mind and in deed from the turbulent converse of the world, that you may be able to see the king

headnotes.la: Videte Dominum Christum in humanitate, quam de virgine matre susceptam in majestatis paternae dextera collocavit
headnotes.en: See the Lord Christ in the humanity which, taken from his virgin mother, he set at the right hand of the Father's majesty

headnotes.la: Id est in tempore incarnationis illius, quo ad copulandam sibi Ecclesiam sponsam ex virginali utero processit
headnotes.en: That is, in the time of his incarnation, in which he came forth from the virginal womb to join to himself the Church as bride

headnotes.la: …rum turpium cultu, ad unum verum Deum conversae Ecclesiae geminam ejus pulchritudinem laudat. Pulchram dixit Ecclesiam, et pulchram repetit, quia hanc et praedicatione et actione vidit esse laudabilem
headnotes.en: …sh, and turned from the worship of many foul gods to the one true God. He called the Church beautiful, and he repeats "beautiful," because he saw her to be praiseworthy both in preaching and in action

headnotes.la: Sensus tui, inquit, spiritualium sunt rerum contemplatione excellentes ac verecundi. Seu oculi, sancti doctores decus populi intelliguntur
headnotes.en: Thy senses, he says, are excellent in the contemplation of spiritual things, and modest. Or by the eyes the holy teachers are understood, the glory of the people

headnotes.la: Magna est quippe gloria aperti operis, sed longe inoptabilior aeternae retributionis, quae necdum videri potest
headnotes.en: Great indeed is the glory of open work, but far more undesirable is that of the eternal recompense, which cannot yet be seen

headnotes.la: …nt, solidum cibum mandendo aliis impertiunt. Qui ascenderunt de lavacro, id est fonte sacri baptismatis, qui et tonsi et loti sunt, hoc est, nudati rebus renuntiantes saeculo, et vitae lavacro mundati
headnotes.en: …Which have come up from the washing, that is, from the font of holy baptism — who are both shorn and washed, that is, stripped of their goods, renouncing the world, and cleansed by the washing of life

headnotes.la: Id est gemina charitate, vel fide et opere fecundi
headnotes.en: That is, fruitful with a twofold charity, or with faith and work

headnotes.la: … assimilantur, quia Dominici sanguinis pretium quo redempta est praedicare non cessat, et in praedicatione ab ardore sanctae charitatis flammescit, et auditores suos in dilectione Dei ardentes efficit
headnotes.en: …cause she does not cease to preach the price of the Lord's blood by which she was redeemed, and in preaching she blazes with the ardor of holy charity, and makes her hearers burning in the love of God

headnotes.la: …i sunt praedicatores, quorum et constantia eadem civitas firma est, et undique inexpugnabilis. Propugnacula autem ejusdem civitatis Scripturarum sacrarum munimina sunt, vel patrum precedentium exempla
headnotes.en: …es, by whose constancy that same city is both firm and on every side unconquerable. But the bulwarks of that same city are the defenses of the holy Scriptures, or the examples of the preceding fathers

headnotes.la: Quia quot in divinis libris praecepta sunt, tot sunt nostri pectoris munimina, quibus contra insidias omnes defendimur
headnotes.en: Because as many as are the precepts in the divine books, so many are the defenses of our breast, by which we are defended against all snares

headnotes.la: …iversus ostenditur, quia universa nostra munitio in sacro eloquio continetur. Ibi quippe sunt praecepta Dei, ibi exempla justorum. Si enim torpet animus a Conditoris suo desiderio, audiat quod dicitur
headnotes.en: …rtification is contained in sacred utterance. For there are the precepts of God, there the examples of the just. For if the soul grows sluggish from the desire of its Creator, let it hear what is said

headnotes.la: et reliqua. In odio fortasse labitur proximi, audiat quod dicitur
headnotes.en: and the rest. Perhaps it slips into hatred of its neighbor: let it hear what is said

headnotes.la: Res alienas concupiscit, audiat quod illic scriptum est
headnotes.en: It covets the goods of others: let it hear what is written there

headnotes.la: De injuria quae a proximi ore vel facto illata est ad iram mens accenditur, audiat quod dicitur
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *domum proximi tui*, "the house of thy neighbor"] The mind is kindled to anger over an injury inflicted by a neighbor's mouth or deed: let it hear what is said

headnotes.la: In carnis concupiscentia male sauciata mens accenditur, ne sequatur oculus mentem, audiat quod dictum est
headnotes.en: The mind, ill-wounded, is kindled in the concupiscence of the flesh; lest the eye follow the mind, let it hear what was said

headnotes.la: Contra inimicum forsitan quisque animum suum relaxare disponit in odio, audiat quod illic scriptum est
headnotes.en: Perhaps someone purposes to let his soul loose in hatred against an enemy: let him hear what is written there

headnotes.la: et reliqua. Sed is qui aliena jam non rapit, adhuc forsitan inordinate retinet, audiat quod illic dicitur
headnotes.en: and the rest. But he who now seizes not the goods of others, yet perhaps still holds them in a disordered way: let him hear what is said there

headnotes.la: Infirmantis animus qui perfrui desiderat Deo simul et saeculo, audiat quod illic scriptum est
headnotes.en: The soul of one growing weak, who desires to enjoy God and the world at once: let it hear what is written there

headnotes.la: Alius non ad necessitatem stipendii, sed ad voluntatem desiderii possessa retinet, audiat quod illic dicitur
headnotes.en: Another keeps his possessions not for the necessity of a livelihood, but for the will of desire: let him hear what is said there

headnotes.la: …anctorum exemplis vel doctrinis. De quibus superius tanquam ex armatura fortium disputatum legimus. Donec aspiret dies aeternus, et transeant umbrae vitae praesentis. Et hinc jam superius disputavimus
headnotes.en: …ch we read that it was discussed above, as it were from the armor of valiant men. Till the eternal day break, and the shadows of the present life pass away. And of this we have already discussed above

headnotes.la: Hoc est quod ait Apostolus [n: (Eph. V)]
headnotes.en: This is what the Apostle says [n: (Eph. V)]

headnotes.la: malae operationis,
headnotes.en: of evil working,

headnotes.la: …tio hortatur sponsus ut veniat. Primo adveniens in carne per bona opera, secundo absoluta carne ad percipiendam vitam aeternam, tertio recepto corpore ad perfruenda post resurrectionem gaudia perfecta
headnotes.en: …o come. First, coming in the flesh through good works; second, released from the flesh to receive eternal life; third, the body having been taken back, to enjoy the perfect joys after the resurrection

headnotes.la: In vulneratione cordis magnitudo amoris Christi in Ecclesia intelligitur
headnotes.en: In the wounding of the heart the greatness of Christ's love in the Church is understood

headnotes.la: …m, et in uno crine colli tui, id est in unitate pia subjectae plebis, id est crinium. Item: In illo itaque oculo Ecclesiae Christo complacuit, quo non temporalia, sed aeterna conspexit. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: …nity of the subject people, that is, of the hairs. Again: With that eye, therefore, the Church was pleasing to Christ, with which she looked not on temporal things, but on eternal. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. XXVI)]
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. XXVI)]

headnotes.la: In mammarum nomine, sancti doctores propter consolationem infirmorum et parvulorum sustentationem exprimuntur. Suavitas gratiae pulchrior est austeritate legis
headnotes.en: …the name of breasts the holy teachers are expressed, on account of the consolation of the weak and the sustaining of little ones. The sweetness of grace is more beautiful than the austerity of the law

headnotes.la: …ona, quae odori Ecclesiae, id est gratiae Spiritus sancti, seu virtutibus comparantur pulcherrimis. Perseverat semper sponsus vices reddendo Ecclesiae, sicut eum Ecclesia laudaverat superius. Ideo ait
headnotes.en: …s, to the grace of the Holy Spirit, or to her most beautiful virtues. The Bridegroom continues always to render like for like to the Church, just as the Church had praised him above. Therefore he says

headnotes.la: …ivinorum eloquiorum sensus in littera. Mel ceram distillat, quia multiplices sensus pene singulae pariunt sententiae. Labia sponsae sunt doctores, qui multifarios sensus sacris litteris inesse pandunt
headnotes.en: …honey drips from the wax, because almost every single sentence brings forth manifold senses. The lips of the bride are the teachers, who lay open the manifold senses that lie within the sacred letters

headnotes.la: In lacte eruditio parvulorum, in melle fortior doctrina perfectorum signatur. Sub lingua, id est in meditatione cordis. Non est necesse subnectere, quid inde Paulus apostolus loquatur
headnotes.en: …little ones, in the honey the stronger doctrine of the perfect is signified. Under the tongue, that is, in the meditation of the heart. There is no need to subjoin what Paul the Apostle says thereupon

headnotes.la: …ed modica, et ideo humiles spiritu designat. Item cinnamomum, qui seipsos decipiunt, signat, et ipsa est arbor brevis, sed odorifera et dulcis. Sic humilitas magnam habet apud eum laudem et dulcedinem
headnotes.en: …erefore it designates the humble in spirit. Again cinnamon signifies those who deceive themselves, and it too is a low tree, but fragrant and sweet. So humility has great praise and sweetness with him

headnotes.la: Sicut fistula et cinnamomum humiles sanctorum cogitationes, sic et ligna Libani sublimes eorum actiones designant
headnotes.en: As sweet cane and cinnamon designate the humble thoughts of the saints, so also the trees of Libanus designate their lofty actions

headnotes.la: …te currit, Christus intelligi secundum humanitatem, per puteum qui occultam habet aquam atque profundissimam, idem ipsum secundum divinitatem. De quo impetu aquae fluunt, ut ipse in Evangelio testatur
headnotes.en: …rstood according to his humanity; by the well, which has hidden and most deep water, the same according to his divinity. From whom the waters flow with force, as he himself bears witness in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …s est calidus, et terram a frigoribus absolvere dicitur, sanctus intimatur Spiritus. Qui flando, id est suis sanctam illustrando Ecclesiam donis, facit illam id diversis germinare virtutibus. Bene ait
headnotes.en: …to loose the earth from the frosts, the Holy Spirit is intimated. Who by blowing, that is, by enlightening his holy Church with his gifts, makes her to bud it forth in divers virtues. Well does he say

headnotes.la: Id est veniat Christus in Ecclesiam suam, et eam ipse conservet ubique immaculatam, et fidei fructu fecundet, et libenter inspiciat, gratanterque accipiat opera sanctorum suorum
headnotes.en: That is, let Christ come into his Church, and himself keep her everywhere unspotted, and make her fruitful with the fruit of faith, and gladly look upon and thankfully receive the works of his saints

headnotes.la: Haec vox non est imperantis, sed indicantis praeteriti temporis. Ac si diceret: Veni, inquit, saepissime in Ecclesiam meam et venio ut corrigam, adjuvem et confirmem, sicuti poposcisti
headnotes.en: …ce of one commanding, but of one declaring a past time. As if he were to say: I have come, he says, most often into my Church, and I come to correct, to help and to confirm, even as thou hast besought

headnotes.la: Per myrrham passio vel mortificatio, per aromata omnes virtutes exprimuntur. Metit myrrham cum aromatibus, quoniam martyres cum caeteris electis ad maturitatem praemiorum perducit
headnotes.en: …cation; by the aromatical spices, all the virtues are expressed. He reaps the myrrh with the aromatical spices, since he leads the martyrs, with the rest of the elect, to the ripeness of their rewards

headnotes.la: In favo et vino praedicatores, in melle et lacte auditores intelliguntur, et utrisque internus judex est qui probat et remunerat
headnotes.en: In the honeycomb and the wine the preachers are understood, in the honey and the milk the hearers, and over both is the inward judge who proves and rewards

headnotes.la: …c si aperte dicat: Amici faciendo quae praecipio. Charissimi, integra charitate amplectendo. Obsecro itaque factis sanctorum, quasi epulis praecipuis, praecordia vestra replete. Cui respondit Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …he things I command. Dearly beloved, by embracing with whole charity. I beseech you therefore, fill your inward parts with the deeds of the saints, as with choice banquets. To whom the Church answered

headnotes.la: …im omnipotens Deus jam in sua claritate conspicitur, sed quiddam sub illa speculatur anima, unde refota proficiat, et post ad visionis ejus gloriam pertingat. Potest et haec vox ad apostolos intelligi
headnotes.en: …ul discerns something beneath that brightness, whereby, being refreshed, it may advance, and afterward attain to the glory of his vision. This voice can also be understood as addressed to the apostles

headnotes.la: …es per sanguinem Christi. Amica, quia est arcanis illius conscia sive per dilectionem, quia servat quae jubentur. Columba, quia Spiritus sancti dono illustrata. Immaculata, quia sola aspectu Dei digna
headnotes.en: …s secrets, or through love, because she keeps the things that are commanded. Dove, because she is enlightened by the gift of the Holy Spirit. Undefiled, because she alone is worthy of the sight of God

headnotes.la: Ac si aperte dicat: Deserui negotia saecularia tui causa, quomodo repetam illa?
headnotes.en: As if she were to say openly: I have forsaken worldly business for thy sake, how shall I seek it again?

headnotes.la: … vel tenebrarum operibus obfuscantur, velut guttis noctium praegravati, Christo quasi adhaerere videntur. Sed quia eumdem Christum non sincere annuntiant, propterea pro talibus ingemiscens subsequitur
headnotes.en: …ss, weighed down as with the drops of the nights, they seem as it were to cleave to Christ. But because they do not sincerely announce that same Christ, therefore, groaning for such men, there follows

headnotes.la: …punctione ad opus virtutum accendit, atque per arctam et angustam viam ad regna coelorum transire docet, nobisque in memoriam revocat quomodo et quanta de sinu patris descendens pro nobis esset passus
headnotes.en: …rtues, and teaches us to pass through the strait and narrow way to the kingdoms of heaven, and calls back to our memory how and how greatly he suffered for us, coming down from the bosom of the Father

headnotes.la: Ecclesia pessulum sponso aperuit: quia templum sui pectoris divina visitatione et inhabitatione dignum facit
headnotes.en: The Church opened the bolt to the Bridegroom, because she makes the temple of her breast worthy of the divine visitation and indwelling

headnotes.la: Quia nulli in hac vita plena visio Dei, sicut in futuro conceditur, ideo transire dicitur, quia in futuro se videndum et perfruendum plenius ostendit
headnotes.en: … to no one in this life is the full vision of God granted, as it is in the life to come, therefore he is said to pass by, because in the life to come he shows himself more fully to be seen and enjoyed

headnotes.la: …sia in admiratione sui stuporis. Quanto suavius, inquit, vocem atque propinquitatem dilecti mei accepi, tanto sublimius quidquid in me erat frigidum, charitate incaluit, et quidquid rigidum, liquefuit
headnotes.en: … her amazement. The more sweetly, she says, I received the voice and the nearness of my beloved, the more loftily did whatever was cold in me grow warm with charity, and whatever was rigid melted away

headnotes.la: …i me, ut amorem quo te languescere dicis mihi ostendas, et qualis sit dilectus tuus ex dilecto, id est Filius ex Patre, Deus ex Deo, et ex ea qua possit parte diligi et non timeri, manifestes. quoniam
headnotes.en: …ich thou sayest thou languishest, and make manifest what manner of one thy beloved is of the beloved, that is, the Son of the Father, God of God, and in what part he may be loved and not feared. since

headnotes.la: Dilectus Ecclesiae, Christus candidus est, quia sine peccato. Aliter: Candidus dicitur, secundum id quod
headnotes.en: The beloved of the Church, Christ, is white, because without sin. Otherwise: He is called white according to that word,

headnotes.la: Rubicundus, quia
headnotes.en: Ruddy, because

headnotes.la: Caput Christi Deus. Sicut inter metalla nihil melius auro, ita nec in creaturis quidquam comparabitur Creatori, quia solus bonus est et optimus
headnotes.en: The head of Christ is God. As among metals nothing is better than gold, so neither among creatures shall anything be compared to the Creator, because he alone is good and best

headnotes.la: Comae Christi catervae sunt sanctorum, quae Deo fideli famulatu adhaerent. Elatae palmae, juxta illud Apostoli
headnotes.en: The locks of Christ are the companies of the saints, which cleave to God in faithful service. Branches of palm, according to that word of the Apostle

headnotes.la: Id est sancti doctores per quos Ecclesia videt quae recta sunt: Qui bene columbae propter simplicitatem et innocentiam comparantur, et rivulis aquarum propter charismata divina
headnotes.en: …oly teachers, through whom the Church sees the things that are right: who are well compared to doves on account of simplicity and innocence, and to brooks of waters on account of the divine free gifts

headnotes.la: … quae ab apostolis in primordiis crediderunt, et ex sancta conversatione ad donum virtutum velut areola aromatum ex se perduxerunt, quae a piis scilicet praedicatoribus consitae, id est eruditae sunt,
headnotes.en: …a holy manner of life brought forth from themselves, as it were a bed of aromatical spices, unto the gift of the virtues; which beds were set, that is, instructed, by devout preachers, that is to say,

headnotes.la: etc. Manus opera sunt illius, quia quae verbis docuit factis implevit. Tornatiles aureae, quia in se omnem regulam justitiae tenent, ut ipse dicit
headnotes.en: etc. His hands are his works, because what he taught in words he fulfilled in deeds. Turned and golden, because they hold in themselves the whole rule of justice, as he himself says

headnotes.la: …nteae fabricatae sunt, in significatione doctorum, qui fabricam Ecclesiae sustentant. Fundati super bases aureas, hoc est praecedentium patrum praedicationem, et per libros legis et Evangelii roborati
headnotes.en: …ation of the teachers who uphold the fabric of the Church. Set upon bases of gold, that is, upon the preaching of the preceding fathers, and strengthened through the books of the law and of the Gospel

headnotes.la: Ut Libanus celsitudine et gratia arborum alios montes, sic nimirum Dominus Christus omnes sanctos meritorum celsitudine, et gratia virtutum antecellit
headnotes.en: As Libanus excels the other mountains in loftiness and in the grace of its trees, so assuredly the Lord Christ excels all the saints in the loftiness of merits and in the grace of virtues

headnotes.la: …id amplius quaeris? Totus desiderabilis, quia totus Deus et totus homo est, in quem desiderant angeli prospicere. Deus in majestate Patris, homo in virginitate matris: in illa Creator, in hac Salvator
headnotes.en: …vely, because he is wholly God and wholly man, on whom the angels desire to look. God in the majesty of the Father, man in the virginity of his mother: in the one the Creator, in the other the Saviour

headnotes.la: …, sed pulcherrima est universitas totius sanctae Ecclesiae per totum orbem. Aliter: Recte enim sancta Ecclesia pulcherrima mulierum appellatur, quia virgo et incorrupta est, cui Apostolus loquens, ait
headnotes.en: …the entire holy Church throughout the whole world. Otherwise: For rightly is holy Church called most beautiful among women, because she is a virgin and uncorrupted, to whom the Apostle, speaking, says

headnotes.la: …rminaret. Aliter: Dilectus Ecclesiae, Christus, descendit in hortum suum, quando visitavit priorem populum suum. Areolam aromatis ipsam sanctam Mariam virginem, de qua secundum carnem natus est, dicit
headnotes.en: …beloved of the Church, Christ, came down into his garden when he visited his former people. By the little bed of spice he means holy Mary the Virgin herself, of whom he was born according to the flesh

headnotes.la: Id est, ut regnet in gentibus seu in Ecclesiis delectetur, ut ex eis virgines quasque vel sanctos assumat. Aliter
headnotes.en: That is, that he may reign among the nations, or take his delight in the Churches, that out of them he may take to himself virgins and saints. Otherwise

headnotes.la: … Hierusalem dicitur, quia ejus vita et desiderium visioni jam pacis intimae comparantur, ut in eo quod auctorem suum diligit, quod ejus speciem videre concupiscit, de quo scriptum est [n: (I Petr. I)]
headnotes.en: …ecause her life and her desire are already compared to the vision of inmost peace, so that in this — that she loves her author, that she longs to see his beauty, of whom it is written [n: (I Petr. I)]

headnotes.la: … reservatur. Aliter vero sentitur, ac si diceret: Nonne semper in corpore conspiciendum requiras, quem semper per fidem melius cernis? Idcirco etenim in coelum ascendi, ut semper tibi localis appaream
headnotes.en: …hou not always seek him to be beheld in the body, whom thou always discernest better through faith? For this cause indeed I ascended into heaven, that I might always appear to thee as bound to a place

headnotes.la: …abiles et moribus venerabiles, et in Christi cruce gloriari non erubescentes. Et.haec magna sunt valde quae videntur in ea, sed multo majora quae non videntur, et in futurum reservantur. Unde Propheta
headnotes.en: …d to glory in the cross of Christ. [sic: *Et.haec*] which are seen in her are exceedingly great, but far greater are those which are not seen, and are reserved for the time to come. Whence the Prophet

headnotes.la: …ti Jerusalem, quae est mater omnium nostrum, unde ad nos gratia Spiritus sancti descendit per quam renascimur Deo. Una vero dicitur, quia, expulsis cunctis reprobis, ipsa tantummodo sociabitur Christo
headnotes.en: …hence the grace of the Holy Spirit descends to us, through which we are born again to God. And she is called one because, when all the reprobate have been cast out, she alone shall be joined to Christ

headnotes.la: …esiae ex gentibus, eo quod sine judiciis legis et instructione prophetarum ad praedicationem Evangelii tam subito tanta perfectione virtutum excreverit, sicut superius admirata jam fuerat. Ait namque.
headnotes.en: …e law and the instruction of the prophets, she had grown up at the preaching of the Gospel so suddenly and with so great a perfection of virtues, even as she had already marvelled above. For she says.

headnotes.la: …quasi aurora, quia jam veri luminis in ea sol ortus mundo post tenebras longae ignorantiae monstratur, vel quando relinquens post se tenebrarum opera caste et sobrie vivit, et ad perfectum diem tendit
headnotes.en: …t is shown to have risen in her upon the world after the darkness of long ignorance; or when, leaving behind her the works of darkness, she lives chastely and soberly, and tends toward the perfect day

headnotes.la: quia a sole justitiae illustrata, noctem mundi illuminat
headnotes.en: because, illumined by the sun of justice, she lights up the night of the world

headnotes.la: quia imaginem sui Conditoris in omni justitiae sanctitate et veritate portat. Aliter
headnotes.en: because she bears the image of her Creator in all justice, holiness, and truth. Otherwise

headnotes.la: per virtutem in praesenti saeculo et decorem
headnotes.en: through virtue and comeliness in the present world

headnotes.la: in futura beatitudine. Vel
headnotes.en: in the blessedness to come. Or

headnotes.la: in conjugatis
headnotes.en: in the married;

headnotes.la: …fructus bonorum, quive adhuc indigeant doctrinae irrigatione. Potest et hortus nucum canon Novi ac Veteris Testamenti designari: in quo sub tegmine litterae velut sub cortice spiritualis latet sensus,
headnotes.en: …ing of doctrine. The garden of nuts may also be taken to designate the canon of the New and the Old Testament: in which, under the covering of the letter, as under a rind, the spiritual sense lies hid

headnotes.la: Id est, si plebs fidelis in studio virtutum floruisset
headnotes.en: That is, if the faithful people had flourished in the pursuit of the virtues

headnotes.la: …m in ea videbis. Potest et aliter intelligi *nescivi.* Anima mea conturbavit me, propter quadrigas Amminadab. Quid nescivit Christus, nisi peccatum? Nescivit illos etiam quibus in judicio dicturus est
headnotes.en: …*I knew not* may also be understood otherwise. My soul troubled me, because of the chariots of Amminadab. What did Christ not know, save sin? He knew not those also to whom he will say in the judgment

headnotes.la: …is ista Ecclesiam significat, cujus figuram Sunamitis illa in libro Regum gestavit. Qui ob hoc qui Christi sanguine decoratur, coccinea in Latino sonat cui frequenter a sanctis praedicatoribus dicitur
headnotes.en: …e figure that Sunamitess in the book of Kings bore. Which for this cause, which is adorned with the blood of Christ, sounds in the Latin *scarlet*; to whom it is frequently said by the holy preachers,

headnotes.la: ut etiamsi per adversa deliquerit, in desperationem non decidat, sed a peccandi consuetudine cum spe indulgentiae resipiscat
headnotes.en: that even if through adversities she has fallen away, she may not sink down into despair, but may come to her senses out of the habit of sinning, with hope of pardon

headnotes.la: …siae ab ipso sponso proferuntur, et primo operum constantia, et mortificatio voluptatum laudantur in ea quam et filiam principis, id est Christi, ob gratiam baptismatis et nobilitatem virtutum nominat
headnotes.en: …of her works and the mortification of pleasures are praised in her, whom also he names the daughter of the prince, that is of Christ, on account of the grace of baptism and the nobility of her virtues

headnotes.la: …In his ergo reperiuntur quae sunt vasa utilia: in eo tornatilis, quia ad obediendum vel ad omne opus bonum semper parati. In eo nunquam indigens poculis, quantum sancti Spiritus gratia ex toto repleti
headnotes.en: …ul vessels: in this it is turned, because they are always ready for obedience and for every good work. In this it never wants cups, inasmuch as they are wholly filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit

headnotes.la: …us. Potest et in collo notitia sacrarum Scripturarum designari, quae idcirco turris eburnea appellatur, quia qui verbo Dei insistunt, quotidiano profectu per nitorem justitiae in excelsiora proficiunt
headnotes.en: …of the Holy Scriptures, which is therefore called a tower of ivory, because those who apply themselves to the word of God, by daily progress advance to loftier things through the brightness of justice

headnotes.la: …etitia carnis, cingulo abstinentiae constringuntur. Et bene in portis filiae multitudinis, ob abundantiam populorum concurrentium per portam fidei in Ecclesiam. Potest et per portam Christus intelligi
headnotes.en: …. And well, in the gates of the daughter of the multitude, because of the abundance of the peoples running together through the gate of faith into the Church. By the gate Christ also may be understood

headnotes.la: …, suis porrigunt auditoribus, atque intellectu discretionis inter odorem virtutum et vitiorum fetores ex alto discernunt. Turri assimilantur, qui per sapientiam eminentissimum locum tenent in Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …tanding of discernment distinguish from on high between the odor of the virtues and the stenches of the vices. They are likened to a tower, who through wisdom hold the most eminent place in the Church

headnotes.la: Pulchra dicitur Ecclesia, fide et opere. Decora ornamentis virtutum. Charissima per dilectionem
headnotes.en: The Church is called beautiful, in faith and in work. Comely, by the ornaments of the virtues. Dearest, through love

headnotes.la: Apte enim victoriosissima crux palmae comparatur, in quam Christus ascendens apprehendit fructum ejus. Illi enim in palmam ascendunt qui in cruce Christi proficiunt. De quo Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: …ittingly is the most victorious cross compared to a palm, into which Christ, going up, took hold of its fruit. For they go up into the palm who advance in the cross of Christ. Whereof the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …inavit, id est sanctos doctores, qui majore scientia et gratia post crucem et resurrectionem Salvatoris abundabant. Possunt et ubera praedicatores Ecclesiae qui renascentes in fide nutriunt, intelligi
headnotes.en: … the cross and resurrection of the Savior abounded in greater knowledge and grace. By the breasts may also be understood the preachers of the Church, who nourish those that are born again in the faith

headnotes.la: In gutture vox praesentis doctrinae, in odore fama absentis designatur. Et ideo vino illa propter flagrantiam virtutum, haec malis, propter suavitatem absentis famae, comparantur
headnotes.en: …of teaching present, in the odor the fame of it absent. And therefore the one is compared to wine, because of the fragrance of the virtues, the other to apples, because of the sweetness of absent fame

headnotes.la: …: possunt in gutture illi intelligi qui per evangelicam praedicationem corda auditorum inebriant: unde Christus potatur, cum ex ea Christiani, qui membra ipsius sunt, incomparabili dulcedine satiantur
headnotes.en: …erstood those who through evangelical preaching inebriate the hearts of the hearers: whence Christ is drunk, when out of her the Christians, who are his members, are filled with incomparable sweetness

headnotes.la: et non alteri cui totam curam servitutis et dilectionis impendo
headnotes.en: and to no other, upon whom I bestow the whole care of my service and of my love

headnotes.la: id est, me solam diligit, et adjuvat me, ne deficiam in via. Cui dilecto ex voce Ecclesiae per Psalmistam dicitur
headnotes.en: that is, he loves me alone, and helps me, that I fail not in the way. To which beloved it is said by the Psalmist in the voice of the Church

headnotes.la: …exercitio bonae operationis persistendo commorari, vel saltem ad propositum bene agendi assurgere, vel animos auditorum suorum quantum profecerint discernere sufficit, nisi Dei gratia adjuta qui dixit
headnotes.en: …ting in the exercise of good working, or even to rise up to the purpose of acting well, or to discern how far the minds of her hearers have advanced, unless she be helped by the grace of God, who said

headnotes.la: …onuntiant. Si floruerunt mala Punica, si illi qui in Christo crediderunt in tanta dilectione proficiunt, ut etiam pro ipso occidi delectentur. His enim singulis sponsa dilecti sui poenitentiam quaerit
headnotes.en: …e pomegranates have flourished, if they who have believed in Christ so advance in love that they even delight to be slain for him. For in each one of these the bride seeks the penitence of her beloved

headnotes.la: …itiorum infirmitatibus sanentur, ostenduntur. Portae Ecclesiae doctores sunt sancti, et in hujusmodi portis mandragorae dant odorem, cum spirituales quique ex se virtutum palmam longe lateque spargunt
headnotes.en: … souls. The gates of the Church are the holy doctors, and in gates of this sort the mandrakes give their odor, when all spiritual men spread abroad from themselves far and wide the palm of the virtues

headnotes.la: Vox ista est antiquorum virorum optantium adventum Christi in carne et illum in Synagoga nasci ac nutriri, juxta humanae conditionis naturam
headnotes.en: …f my mother"] This is the voice of the men of old, desiring the coming of Christ in the flesh, and that he should be born and nourished in the Synagogue, according to the nature of the human condition

headnotes.la: Intus erat dilectus, dum
headnotes.en: Within was the beloved, while

headnotes.la: foris, dum
headnotes.en: ; without, while

headnotes.la: facie ad faciem videam, et ore ad os loquar. De quo osculo in exordio libri satis arbitror dictum
headnotes.en: : that I may see face to face, and speak mouth to mouth. Of which kiss I think enough has been said at the opening of the book

headnotes.la: Ante adventum Christi intra angustias Judaeae tantum fuit Ecclesia, post ascensionem in toto mundo dilatata fuit, et venerabilis effecta. Prius dictum fuerat,
headnotes.en: Before the coming of Christ the Church was only within the narrow bounds of Judaea; after the ascension she was spread abroad in the whole world, and made venerable. Before it had been said,

headnotes.la: nunc autem dicitur
headnotes.en: ; but now it is said

headnotes.la: id est prompta ac fideli devotione venientem accipiam
headnotes.en: that is, I will receive thee coming with ready and faithful devotion

headnotes.la: Peracta carnis dispensatione, redeuntem laetis ducam luminibus in domum matris, id est coelestis Hierusalem, quae est mater nostra
headnotes.en: The dispensation of the flesh accomplished, I will lead thee, returning, with joyful eyes into my mother's house, that is of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is our mother

headnotes.la: id est facies me potiora sperare dona, quam in lege habuissem
headnotes.en: that is, thou shalt make me hope for better gifts than I had had in the law

headnotes.la: id est ferventem amorem variis virtutum pigmentis odoratum vel ornatum
headnotes.en: that is, a fervent love made fragrant or adorned with the various pigments of the virtues

headnotes.la: …e transire non dubitant. Aliter: Ducit Ecclesia Christum in domum matris coelestis Hierusalem, quando cum omnibus bonis quae per suam gratiam consecuta est, etiam ipsa perduci meretur. Ibique docetur,
headnotes.en: …o the house of her mother, the heavenly Jerusalem, when together with all the good things which she has obtained through his grace she also deserves herself to be led thither. And there she is taught,

headnotes.la: … saepe diximus, indicium est, nunc tangamus breviter. Vox Synagogae vel prophetae admirantis, quomodo Ecclesia de deserto gentilitatis in sponsis subito amplexus ascendisset: cui per prophetam dicitur
headnotes.en: … the voice of the Synagogue, or of the prophet, marvelling how the Church had come up so suddenly out of the desert of heathenism into the embraces of the bridegroom: to whom it is said by the prophet

headnotes.la: etc. Et in psalmo
headnotes.en: etc. And in the psalm

headnotes.la: Deliciis affluens, id est omnium donorum pulchritudine
headnotes.en: Flowing with delights, that is, with the beauty of all gifts

headnotes.la: Quia omnia quae habet, ad gratiam ipsius refert stabilita in eo fide, spe et charitate, quem mihi soli committendam credebant
headnotes.en: …xa super dilectum suum*, "upon her beloved"] Because all that she has she refers to his grace, being established in him by faith, hope, and charity — whom they believed was to be committed to me alone

headnotes.la: Respondit sponsa pro Synagoga. Ipse sponsus sub arbore crucis a perpetua morte liberavi te, ut apostolos et caeteros electos ex Judaea
headnotes.en: The bride answered on behalf of the Synagogue. I, the bridegroom himself, under the tree of the cross freed thee from perpetual death, as I freed the apostles and the rest of the elect out of Judaea

headnotes.la: Signaculum in brachio vel digito, ob memoriam cuilibet rei ligamus. Per
headnotes.en: A seal we bind upon the arm or the finger for the remembrance of some matter. By

headnotes.la: cogitatio, et per
headnotes.en: thought is designated, and by

headnotes.la: … auferri pertimescas, ut tam cogitatione quam etiam operatione ad illud signum recurras, et sicut ego te intantum dilexi, ut mori voluissem pro te, ita econtrario sancti tui mortem non recusent pro me
headnotes.en: …hat both in thought and also in working thou mayest run back to that sign; and as I have so loved thee that I was willing to die for thee, so, on the other hand, let thy saints not refuse death for me

headnotes.la: Fortis est usque ad mortem dilectio mea in te, o Synagoga, sed tua aemulatio dura in me fuit sicut infernus: sed verte aemulationem in dilectionem, et eris mihi sponsa, et soror, et amica
headnotes.en: Strong even unto death is my love toward thee, O Synagogue; but thy jealousy toward me was hard as hell: yet turn thy jealousy into love, and thou shalt be to me bride, and sister, and love

headnotes.la: Aquas multas et flumina, tentationum dicit incursus, quae visibiliter seu invisibiliter animas fidelium impugnant, quibus charitas non cedit
headnotes.en: By many waters and floods he means the onsets of temptations, which visibly or invisibly assail the souls of the faithful, to which charity does not yield

headnotes.la: …ut vero totius substantiae divitias pro dilectionis Christi magnitudine dantes, quasi nihil despiciebant eum, id est mundum. Alio vero modo ex superioribus pendet sententiae sensus. Cum enim dixisset,
headnotes.en: …r whole substance for the greatness of the love of Christ despised it as nothing, that is, the world. But in another manner the sense of the sentence hangs upon what goes before. For when he had said,

headnotes.la: vel flumina
headnotes.en: or floods

headnotes.la: subjunxit
headnotes.en: he subjoined

headnotes.la: etc., ut illuc intelligatur quod Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: etc., so that there may be understood what the Apostle says

headnotes.la: Prima nascentis Ecclesiae de gentibus tempora designat, quoniam adhuc et parva fuit numero, et minus idonea praedicare verbum, ut Apostolus loquitur
headnotes.en: …arva*, "Our sister is little"] It designates the first times of the Church newly born out of the nations, since as yet she was both small in number and less fit to preach the word, as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: Quasi vox sponsi vel apostolorum, de ipsa ad Synagogam dixisset
headnotes.en: As it were the voice of the bridegroom, or of the apostles, had said of her to the Synagogue

headnotes.la: …e fortes in fide, vel claros ingenio, vel philosophia instructos, addamus illis propugnacula argentea, id est scientiam divinarum Scripturarum, ut eo facilius possint protegere infirmos atque indoctos
headnotes.en: … talent, or instructed in philosophy, let us add to them bulwarks of silver, that is the knowledge of the divine Scriptures, that they may be able the more easily to protect the weak and the unlearned

headnotes.la: Id est, si sint simplices, tamen docendi studio inhiantes, et velut ostium quod aperitur et clauditur,
headnotes.en: That is, if they be simple, yet gaping with zeal for being taught, and, like a door which is opened and shut, understand

headnotes.la: …mus illis priorum exempla justorum, quo certius et efficacius docendi officium implere possint. Cedri virtutes sanctorum, et tabulae latitudinem designant charitatis. Et ut cum Apostolo dicere valeant
headnotes.en: … the more surely and effectually fulfil the office of teaching. The cedars designate the virtues of the saints, and the boards the breadth of charity. And that they may be able to say with the Apostle

headnotes.la: De quo Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *quae habet populos*, "which hath peoples"] Whereof the Apostle says

headnotes.la: Et de quo propheta
headnotes.en: And whereof the prophet

headnotes.la: …rris, in ea congregatione qua multos populos possidet ex toto orbe, non in Judaea solum, tradidit eam custodibus, sed et prophetis vel apostolis sive evangelicis dogmatibus, vel angelicis dignitatibus
headnotes.en: …gation wherein he possesses many peoples out of the whole world, not in Judaea alone; he delivered it to keepers, but also to prophets or apostles, or to evangelical teachings, or to angelic dignities

headnotes.la: Id est Christus appendens regnum coelorum pro sanctis laboribus vel eleemosynis ejus. Potest et aliter intelligi
headnotes.en: That is, Christ weighing out the kingdom of heaven for its holy labors or alms. It may also be understood otherwise

headnotes.la: Vox sponsi, quia post resurrectionem futuram sancti omnes semper cum Domino erunt, sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: It is the voice of the bridegroom, because after the resurrection to come all the saints shall be always with the Lord, as he himself says

headnotes.la: Aliter, ac si diceret sponsus: Verum etsi te aliis commendem custodibus, tamen te semper habeo in mea praesentia, videns et remunerans laboris in omnibus devotionem
headnotes.en: Otherwise, as if the bridegroom said: Truly, even though I commend thee to other keepers, yet I have thee always in my presence, seeing and rewarding in all things the devotion of thy labor

headnotes.la: …i. Quasi dixisset: Qui amore meo cuncta sua dimittit, in pace habere servata cognoscat, significans simpliciores in Ecclesia qui omnem substantiam millenario signatam numero pro charitate Dei amittunt
headnotes.en: …love of me lets go all his own know that he has them kept in peace; signifying the simpler sort in the Church, who lose for the charity of God all their substance, marked with the number of a thousand

headnotes.la: …t angelici spiritus, et animae sanctorum separatae considerant, et de tuo gaudent profectu. Item amici auscultant, quia omnes electi, ut ad coelestem patriam reviviscant, verba vitae audire desiderant
headnotes.en: …s, are considering thee, and rejoice at thy progress. Likewise the friends hearken, because all the elect, that they may come alive again unto the heavenly fatherland, desire to hear the words of life

headnotes.la: Ac si aperte dicat: Quoniam in carne apparens praecepta ac dona vitae mihi deferens, nunc his peractis reverte in sinum Patris: O mi dilecte,
headnotes.en: …f prints] As if she plainly said: Since, appearing in the flesh and bringing to me the precepts and the gifts of life, now, these being accomplished, return into the bosom of the Father: O my beloved,

headnotes.la: … varietatem virtutum dicitur, qui cum qua carne ad coelos ascendit, cum ipsa versatus est in terris. Montes aromatum, angeli intelliguntur, super quos exaltatus est homo assumptus, sicut Psalmista ait
headnotes.en: …e flesh wherewith he ascended into the heavens, with that same dwelt upon earth. By the mountains of spices are understood the angels, above whom the man assumed has been exalted, as the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: Hinc verum dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *in jubilo*] Hence he says truly

headnotes.la: Hinc Lucas ait
headnotes.en: Hence Luke says

headnotes.la: … solerti studio et puritate cordis, et pudicitia corporis nequiveris. Scriptura etenim sacra, ut saepe praefatus tractator ait, mons est de quo in nostris cordibus Dominus venit. De quo propheta dicit
headnotes.en: … by diligent zeal and purity of heart and chastity of body. For Holy Scripture, as the aforesaid expositor often says, is a mountain from which the Lord comes into our hearts. Whereof the prophet says

headnotes.la: …tias, et umbrosus per allegorias. Sed sciendum quia cum vox in monte sonat, vestimenta lavare praecipimur, et ab omni inquinatione carnis mundare, si ad montem festinemus accedere. Scriptum quippe est
headnotes.en: …, when the voice sounds upon the mountain, we are commanded to wash our garments, and to cleanse them from every defilement of the flesh, if we would hasten to approach the mountain. For it is written

headnotes.la: … circa hunc montem visus fuerit, atrocissimis sententiis, veluti lapidibus necatur. Ardet enim iste mons, quia sacra Scriptura quem spiritualiter replet, amoris igne succendit. Unde per Moysen dicitur
headnotes.en: … is slain by most terrible sentences, as it were by stones. For this mountain burns, because Holy Scripture kindles with the fire of love him whom it spiritually fills. Whence it is said through Moses

headnotes.la: …, id est celsitudines angelorum tandem Domino favente adire, atque eorum suffragiis orationum ad dexteram judicis cum sanctis imperatoribus et consulibus collocari merearis, pariterque a Domino audire
headnotes.en: …s of spices, that is the heights of the angels, and by the suffrages of their prayers to be placed at the right hand of the judge with the holy emperors and consuls, and likewise to hear from the Lord
